sentences.zh: 列傳第六十四

translations.literal: Biography 64
translations.idiomatic: Biography 64

sentences.zh: 段文振來護兒樊子蓋周羅碶周法尚衛玄劉權李景薛世雄

translations.literal: Duan Wenzhen, Lai Hu'er, Fan Zigai, Zhou Luohou, Zhou Fashang, Wei Xuan, Liu Quan, Li Jing, Xue Shixiong
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenzhen, Lai Hu'er, Fan Zigai, Zhou Luohou, Zhou Fashang, Wei Xuan, Liu Quan, Li Jing, and Xue Shixiong

sentences.zh: 段文振，北海期原人也。

translations.literal: Duan Wenzhen was a native of Qiyuan in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenzhen came from Qiyuan in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，魏滄州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was Governor of Cangzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou had served as governor of Cangzhou in Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父威，周洮、河、甘、渭四州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wei was Governor of the four provinces Tao, He, Gan, and Wei under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei had held successive governorships over Tao, He, Gan, and Wei under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 文振少有膂力，膽智過人，明達世務。

translations.literal: Wenzhen in youth had great physical strength, courage and wisdom surpassing others, and clear understanding of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wenzhen was powerfully built, bolder and shrewder than most, and keenly versed in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 初為周塚宰宇文護親信，護知其有器局幹用，擢授中外府兵曹。

translations.literal: At first he was a trusted follower of Zhou's regent Yuwen Hu; Hu, knowing his capacity and practical ability, promoted him to military clerk of the central and outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a confidant of the Zhou regent Yuwen Hu, who recognized his talent and administrative skill and appointed him military clerk in the central administration.

sentences.zh: 後從周武帝攻齊海昌王尉相貴于晉州，其亞將侯子欽、崔景嵩為內應，文振杖槊與崔仲方等數十人先登城。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in attacking Qi Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui at Jinyang; Xianggui's lieutenant Hou Ziqin and Cui Jingsong acted as inside agents, and Wenzhen with spear in hand was among several dozen men led by Cui Zhongfang who were first to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning with Emperor Wu of Zhou against the Qi Prince of Haichang, Wei Xianggui, at Jinyang, he joined an assault in which Xianggui's subordinates Hou Ziqin and Cui Jingsong served as inside contacts; Wenzhen took a spear and, with Cui Zhongfang and some dozens of men, was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 文振隨景嵩至相貴所，拔佩刀劫之，相貴不敢動，城遂下。

translations.literal: Wenzhen followed Jingsong to Xianggui's place, drew his girdle knife and seized him; Xianggui dared not move, and the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen went with Jingsong to Xianggui's quarters, drew his sword, and seized him at knifepoint; Xianggui did not dare stir, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 及攻并州，陷東門而入，齊安德王延宗懼而出降。

translations.literal: When they attacked Bingzhou, they broke in through the east gate; Qi Prince of Ande Yan Zong, in fear, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Bingzhou they broke through the east gate; the Qi Prince of Ande, Yan Zong, surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 錄前後勳，將拜柱國，以讒毀獲譴，因授上儀同，賜爵襄國縣公。

translations.literal: His earlier and later merit was recorded; he was about to be enfeoffed as pillar of state, but because of slander he was reprimanded and instead received senior privy counselor, with enfeoffment as Duke of Xiangguo county.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service was entered on the rolls and he was on the point of receiving the rank of pillar of state, but slander brought a reprimand; he was given senior privy counselor instead and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangguo county.

sentences.zh: 進平鄴都，又賜綺羅二千段，後從滕王逌擊稽胡，破之。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify the capital at Ye, he was again granted two thousand lengths of silk gauze; later he followed Prince of Teng You in attacking the Ji barbarians and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Ye and received another grant of two thousand bolts of silk; afterward he followed the Prince of Teng in a campaign against the Ji tribes and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又以天官都上士從韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: Again, as senior clerk of the celestial offices, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in operations in the Huainan region.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as a senior clerk in the celestial offices under Wei Xiaokuan's Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 俄而尉遲迥作亂，時文振老母妻子俱在鄴城，迥遣人誘之，文振不顧。

translations.literal: Soon Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion; at the time Wenzhen's aged mother, wife, and children were all in Ye, and Jiong sent men to entice him, but Wenzhen paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuchi Jiong rebelled; Wenzhen's mother, wife, and children were then all in Ye, and Jiong sent envoys to win him over, but he would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝引為丞相掾。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui summoned him as an aide to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui brought him in as an aide in the chief minister's office.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難之奔陳，文帝令文振安集淮南，還除衛尉少卿，兼內史侍郎。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Emperor Wen ordered Wenzhen to settle and gather the Huainan region; on his return he was appointed vice minister of the guard and concurrently vice director of the inner secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, the emperor sent Wenzhen to restore order in Huainan; on his return he was made vice minister of the guard and concurrent vice director of the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍長史從達奚震討平叛蠻，加上開府，遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Soon, as army campaign chief clerk, he followed Daxi Zhen in suppressing rebellious barbarians; he was given supernumerary grand opening and promoted to minister of guests.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as chief clerk on campaign with Daxi Zhen against rebel tribes, received the supernumerary grand opening rank, and was promoted to minister of guests.

sentences.zh: 衛王爽北征突厥，以文振為長史，坐勳簿不實免官。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wei Shuang campaigned north against the Turks, Wenzhen was made chief clerk; because the merit register was not truthful he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: On the Prince of Wei's northern expedition against the Turks he served as chief clerk, but was dismissed when his merit register was found false.

sentences.zh: 後為石、河二州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Later he was governor of the two provinces Shi and He, and had great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Shi and He provinces, where his authority and benevolence were widely felt.

sentences.zh: 遷蘭州總管，改封龍岡縣公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be regional commander of Lanzhou and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Longgang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Lanzhou and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Longgang county.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以行軍總管擊破之，遂北至居延塞。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, as campaign commander he defeated them and then advanced north as far as the Juyan pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the border he routed them as campaign commander and pushed north to the Juyan frontier.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，大舉伐陳，為元帥秦王司馬，別領行軍總管，及平江南，授揚州總管司馬，轉并州總管司馬，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, in the great campaign against Chen, he was staff officer to the Prince of Qin, the commander-in-chief, and separately led a campaign command; when the south of the Yangzi was pacified he was appointed staff officer to the regional commander of Yangzhou, then transferred as staff officer to the regional commander of Bingzhou, and left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 9, during the great invasion of Chen, he served as staff officer to the Prince of Qin, the supreme commander, while also leading a campaign force in his own right; after the south was pacified he became staff officer to the Yangzhou commander, then to the Bingzhou commander, and resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後拜雲州總管，遷太僕卿。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed regional commander of Yunzhou and promoted to minister of the stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made regional commander of Yunzhou and then minister of the stud.

sentences.zh: 十九年，突厥犯塞，以行軍總管破達頭可汗于沃野。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the Turks raided the frontier, as campaign commander he defeated Qaghan Datou at Woye.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19, when Turks again raided the frontier, he defeated Qaghan Datou at Woye as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 文振先與王世積有舊。

translations.literal: Wenzhen had earlier been on familiar terms with Wang Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen had long been acquainted with Wang Shiji.

sentences.zh: 初，文振北征，世積遺以駝。

translations.literal: At first, when Wenzhen campaigned north, Shiji sent him camels as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: On his northern campaign Shiji had once sent him camels as a gift.

sentences.zh: 比還，世積以罪誅，文振坐與交關，功遂不錄。

translations.literal: By the time he returned, Shiji had been executed for a crime; Wenzhen was implicated for association with him, and his merit was therefore not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned, Shiji had been executed for treason; Wenzhen was punished for their association, and his achievements went uncredited.

sentences.zh: 後平越巂叛蠻，賜奴婢二百口。

translations.literal: Later he pacified rebellious barbarians in Yuexi and was granted two hundred household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He later suppressed rebel tribes in Yuexi and was rewarded with two hundred slaves.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，嘉州獠反，文振以行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, the Liao of Jiazhou rebelled, and Wenzhen as campaign commander attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era the Liao of Jiazhou rebelled, and Wenzhen was sent against them as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 引軍山谷間，為賊所襲，遂大敗。

translations.literal: He led his army through mountain valleys and was ambushed by bandits, suffering a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Leading his troops through the valleys he was ambushed and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 文振復收散兵，竟破之。

translations.literal: Wenzhen again gathered the scattered troops and in the end defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen rallied his scattered forces and eventually broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 文振性素剛直，無所降下。

translations.literal: Wenzhen's nature had always been stern and upright; he bowed to no one.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Wenzhen was blunt and unyielding; he deferred to no one.

sentences.zh: 初，軍次益州，謁蜀王秀，貌頗不恭，秀甚銜之。

translations.literal: At first, when the army halted at Yizhou, he called on Prince of Shu Xiu with a demeanor rather lacking in respect; Xiu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when his army had halted at Yizhou, he had paid a call on the Prince of Shu, Xiu, with a manner that Xiu found distinctly disrespectful, and the prince bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及此，奏文振師徒喪亂。

translations.literal: On this occasion he memorialized that Wenzhen's army had suffered loss and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now he memorialized that Wenzhen's forces had been routed and disordered.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威與文振有隙，因譖之，坐是除名。

translations.literal: Right vice director Su Wei had a rift with Wenzhen and slandered him on this account; for this reason Wenzhen was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The right vice director Su Wei, who bore a grudge against him, joined in the accusation, and Wenzhen was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢黜，文振上表自申，帝慰諭之，授大將軍，拜靈州總管。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed and removed, Wenzhen submitted a memorial in his own defense; the emperor comforted and instructed him, granted him grand general, and appointed him regional commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu's fall Wenzhen petitioned in his own defense; the emperor reassured him, made him grand general, and appointed him regional commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，徵為兵部尚書，待遇甚重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Wenzhen was summoned as minister of war and treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne he was recalled as minister of war and held in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，文振督兵屯雪山，連營三百餘里，東接楊義臣，西連張壽，合圍渾主于覆袁川以功進位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Tuyuhun, Wenzhen directed troops encamped at Snow Mountain in a continuous line of camps more than three hundred li, joining Yang Yichen in the east and Zhang Shou in the west, and together besieged the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River; for merit he was advanced to right grand master of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he commanded troops along Snow Mountain in a chain of camps stretching more than three hundred li, linking with Yang Yichen in the east and Zhang Shou in the west to surround the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River; for this service he was promoted to right grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，以文振行江都郡事。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, Wenzhen was put in charge of Jiangdu commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, Wenzhen was left to administer the commandery.

sentences.zh: 文振見文帝時容納突厥啟人，居於塞內，妻以公主，賞賜重疊，及大業初，恩澤彌厚，恐為國患。

translations.literal: Wenzhen saw that in Emperor Wen's time the Turks under Qiren had been received and settled within the frontier, given a princess in marriage, and heaped with repeated rewards; by the beginning of Daye the favors had grown still thicker, and he feared they would become a national peril.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen had watched Emperor Wen settle the Turkish Qiren people inside the frontier, marry them to an imperial princess, and shower them with gifts; by the opening years of Daye the favors had only grown, and he feared they would become a grave threat to the state.

sentences.zh: 乃上表請以時喻遣，令出塞外，然後明設烽候，緣邊鎮防，務令嚴重，此乃萬世之長策。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial asking that they be persuaded in due season to depart and sent beyond the frontier, and that beacon towers be clearly set up and frontier garrisons strengthened along the border so that defenses would be strict—this, he said, was a long-term policy for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized that they should be persuaded to withdraw beyond the frontier in good time, that beacon lines and border garrisons should be restored in full strength—a policy, he argued, that would secure the realm for generations.

sentences.zh: 時兵部侍郎斛斯政專掌兵事，文振知政險薄，不可委以機要，屢言於帝。

translations.literal: At the time vice minister of war Husijun alone controlled military affairs; Wenzhen knew Jun was treacherous and shallow and could not be entrusted with crucial matters, and repeatedly spoke to the emperor about it.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of war Husijun then controlled military affairs alone; Wenzhen knew him to be treacherous and unworthy of confidence in critical matters, and warned the emperor repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 帝並弗納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，授左候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign began, he was appointed grand general of the left guard of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he was made grand general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 出南蘇道。

translations.literal: He marched out by the Nansu route.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Nansu route.

sentences.zh: 在軍疾篤，上表以為「遼東小丑，未服嚴刑。

translations.literal: In camp his illness grew grave, and he submitted a memorial saying, "The petty men of Liaodong have not yet submitted to stern punishment.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened in the field, and he submitted a memorial: "The petty rulers of Liaodong have not yet been brought to heel by force.

sentences.zh: 但夷狄多詐，深須防擬，口陳降款，心懷背叛，詭伏多端，勿得便受。

translations.literal: But the barbarians are full of deceit and must be guarded against with the utmost care; though they declare surrender with their mouths, in their hearts they harbor betrayal, and their stratagems and ambushes are many—do not readily accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians are treacherous by nature and must be watched closely: they may offer surrender while plotting revolt, and their ruses are many—do not accept their word too readily.

sentences.zh: 水潦方降，不可淹遲，唯願嚴勒諸軍，星馳速發，則平壤孤城，勢可拔也。

translations.literal: The rains are about to fall and delay must not be allowed; I only wish that all armies be strictly urged to march at star speed, and then the isolated city of Pyongyang can by its situation be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rains will soon come and there must be no delay; I beg that all armies be driven forward at once, for then isolated Pyongyang can surely be taken.

sentences.zh: 若傾其本根，餘城自克。

translations.literal: If their root is overturned, the remaining cities will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Strike at the root and the rest will fall of themselves.

sentences.zh: 如不時定，脫遇秋霖，深為艱弊，兵糧又竭，強敵在前，靺鞨出後，遲疑不決，非上策也」。

translations.literal: If it is not settled in time and we happen to meet autumn rains, the hardship will be deep; army grain will again be exhausted, a strong foe will be before us and the Mohe will emerge behind—hesitation and indecision are not the superior policy."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to finish quickly and autumn rains set in, the hardship will be severe, supplies will run out, a strong enemy will lie ahead and the Mohe will threaten from the rear—hesitation is no sound strategy."

sentences.zh: 卒于師。

translations.literal: He died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝省表，悲歎久之，贈光祿大夫、尚書右僕射、北平公，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and mourned for a long while, posthumously granting grand master of splendid happiness, right vice director of the secretariat, and Duke of Beiping, with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and grieved at length, posthumously granting him grand master of splendid happiness, right vice director of the secretariat, and the title Duke of Beiping, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長子詮，位武牙郎將。

translations.literal: His eldest son Quan held the post of commandant of the martial tusk guard.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Quan served as commandant of the martial tusk guard.

sentences.zh: 次子綸，少以俠氣聞。

translations.literal: His second son Lun was in youth known for chivalrous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Lun was known from youth for his daring spirit.

sentences.zh: 文振弟文操，大業中，為武賁郎將，性甚剛嚴。

translations.literal: Wenzhen's younger brother Wencao, in the Daye era, was a commandant of the martial guard; his nature was very stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen's younger brother Wencao, who in the Daye era served as commandant of the martial guard, was notoriously harsh and rigid.

sentences.zh: 帝令督秘書省學士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to supervise the scholars of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put him in charge of the secretariat scholars.

sentences.zh: 時學士頗存儒雅，文操輒鞭撻之，前後或至千數，時議者鄙之。

translations.literal: At the time the scholars still preserved refined elegance; Wencao would whip and beat them, in some cases reaching a thousand strokes before and after, and men of the age despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars still cultivated scholarly decorum, but Wencao would flog them by the hundreds—on some occasions nearly a thousand strokes—and public opinion held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 來護兒，字崇善，本南陽新野人，漢中郎將歙十八世孫也。

translations.literal: Lai Hu'er, style name Chongshan, was originally a native of Xinye in Nanyang, eighteenth-generation descendant of Han commandant of the palace guards She.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Hu'er, styled Chongshan, was originally from Xinye in Nanyang and claimed descent in the eighteenth generation from the Han palace guard commandant She.

sentences.zh: 曾祖成，魏新野縣侯，後歸梁，徙居廣陵，因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Cheng was Marquis of Xinye county under Wei; later he submitted to Liang, moved to Guangling, and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cheng had been Marquis of Xinye under Wei, later submitted to Liang, moved to Guangling, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 位終六合令。

translations.literal: He ended his career as magistrate of Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as magistrate of Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，步兵校尉、秦郡太守、長寧縣侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ni was commandant of foot soldiers, governor of Qin commandery, and Marquis of Changning county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ni had been commandant of foot soldiers, governor of Qin commandery, and Marquis of Changning county.

sentences.zh: 父法敏，仕陳終於海陵令。

translations.literal: His father Famin served Chen and ended as magistrate of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Famin had served Chen and died as magistrate of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 護兒未識而孤，養于世母吳氏。

translations.literal: Hu'er was orphaned before he could know his parents and was raised by his father's sister-in-law, Lady Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er lost his parents in infancy and was raised by his father's sister-in-law, Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳氏提攜鞠養，甚有慈訓，幼而卓犖，初讀《詩》，至「擊鼓其鏜，踴躍用兵」，「羔裘豹飾，孔武有力」。

translations.literal: Lady Wu brought him up and nurtured him with much kindly instruction; in youth he was outstanding. When he first read the Book of Songs and came to "The drums beat loud, leaping they take up arms" and "Lamb's fur, leopard trim, most martial his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu raised him with devoted care and wise guidance. Even as a boy he stood out. When he first read the Book of Songs and came to the lines about drums sounding for war and a warrior clad in lamb's fur and leopard trim, mighty in strength.

sentences.zh: 因舍書歎曰：「大丈夫在世當如是，會為國滅賊以取功名，安能區區專事筆硯也！」

translations.literal: he therefore put aside the book and sighed, saying, "A great man in the world ought to be like this; he should destroy the state's enemies and win fame—how can he fuss over brush and inkstone alone!
translations.idiomatic: He set the book aside and sighed: "A true man in this world should live like that—he should destroy the state's enemies and win glory. How can he waste his life over brush and inkstone alone!

sentences.zh: 群輩驚其言而壯其志。

translations.literal: His companions were startled at his words and admired his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: His companions were startled by his words and admired his resolve.

sentences.zh: 及長，雄略秀出，志氣英進。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his bold strategy stood out, and his spirit and ambition were lofty and advancing.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured his strategic gifts shone, and his spirit was bold and forward.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書史，不為章句學。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and histories but did not pursue the study of textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in history but cared nothing for pedantic commentary.

sentences.zh: 始，侯景之亂，護兒世父為鄉人陶武子所害，吳氏每流涕為護兒言之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the turmoil of Hou Jing, Hu'er's father's elder brother was killed by a fellow townsman, Tao Wuzi; Lady Wu would weep whenever she spoke of it to Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of Hou Jing's rebellion, Hu'er's uncle had been killed by a townsman named Tao Wuzi; Lady Wu wept whenever she told Hu'er the story.

sentences.zh: 武子宗族數百家，厚自封植。

translations.literal: Wuzi's clan numbered several hundred households and had richly built up its own power.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi's clan numbered several hundred households and had grown powerful through self-aggrandizement.

sentences.zh: 護兒每思復怨，因其有婚禮，乃結客數人，直入其家，引武子斬之，賓客皆懾不敢動。

translations.literal: Hu'er often thought of avenging the grudge; when Wuzi held a wedding, he gathered several guests, went straight into his house, seized Wuzi and beheaded him, and all the guests were terrified and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er brooded on revenge; when Wuzi held a wedding feast he gathered a few companions, burst into the house, seized Wuzi, and cut off his head while the guests stood frozen in terror.

sentences.zh: 乃以其頭祭伯父墓，因潛伏歲餘。

translations.literal: He then offered Wuzi's head at his uncle's tomb and went into hiding for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He offered Wuzi's head at his uncle's tomb and then lay in hiding for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 會周師定淮南，乃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies pacified Huainan, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces pacified Huainan he returned home.

sentences.zh: 所住白土村，地居疆埸，數見軍旅，護兒常慨然有立功名之志。

translations.literal: The village of Baitu where he lived lay on the borderland and often saw armies pass; Hu'er frequently sighed with resolve to establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: His village of Baitu lay on the frontier where armies often passed, and he often burned with ambition to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 及開皇初，宇文忻、宇若弼等鎮廣陵，並深相禮重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Yuwen Xin, Yu Ruobi, and others garrisoned Guangling and all treated him with deep courtesy and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, when Yuwen Xin and Yu Ruobi garrisoned Guangling, they all treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 除大都督，領本鄉兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand commander and led the militia of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander and led the local militia of his district.

sentences.zh: 破陳將曾永，以功授儀同三司，平陳之役，護兒有功焉，進位上開府，賞物一千段。

translations.literal: He defeated the Chen general Zeng Yong and for merit was granted privy counselor of the third rank; in the campaign to pacify Chen, Hu'er had merit, was advanced to supernumerary grand opening, and rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Chen general Zeng Yong and was rewarded with the third rank of privy counselor; in the conquest of Chen he distinguished himself, was promoted to supernumerary grand opening, and received a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 十一年，高智慧據江南反，以子總管統兵隋楊素討之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Gao Zhihui held the south of the Yangzi in rebellion; as subordinate regional commander he commanded troops under Yang Su of Sui to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, when Gao Zhihui rebelled and held the lower Yangzi, he served as subordinate commander under Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 賊據浙江岸為營，周亙百餘里，船艦被江，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: The rebels held camps along the Zhe River bank for more than a hundred li in circuit; their ships covered the river and they advanced with drum and shout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had fortified the Zhe River bank for over a hundred li; their fleet covered the river and they advanced with drums and war cries.

sentences.zh: 護兒言於素曰：「吳人累銳，利在舟楫。

translations.literal: Hu'er said to Su, "The men of Wu have long been sharp; their advantage lies in boats.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er told Su, "The southerners are seasoned fighters and their strength lies in their fleet.

sentences.zh: 必死之賊，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: These are enemies who will fight to the death; it is hard to cross blades with them.
translations.idiomatic: They will fight to the death and are hard to meet head-on on the water.

sentences.zh: 公且嚴陣以待之，勿與接刃，請假奇兵數千，潛度江，掩破其壁，使退無所歸，進不得戰，此韓信破趙之策也。」

translations.literal: My lord, hold a strict formation and wait for them; do not join blades with them. Allow me several thousand picked troops to cross the river in secret, strike and break their ramparts, so that in retreat they have nowhere to return and in advance they cannot fight—this is the stratagem by which Han Xin broke Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Hold your line and do not engage them directly. Give me a few thousand picked men to cross the river in secret and smash their camp, so they can neither retreat nor advance to fight—this is Han Xin's stratagem against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 素以為然。

translations.literal: Su thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed.

sentences.zh: 護兒乃以輕舸數百，直登江岸，襲破其營，因縱火，煙焰張天。

translations.literal: Hu'er then with several hundred light boats went straight to the river bank, stormed and broke their camp, and set fire; smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er took several hundred light boats straight to the bank, stormed the camp, and set it ablaze until smoke and flame filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 賊顧火而懼，素因是動，一鼓破之。

translations.literal: The rebels looked back at the fire and were afraid; Su thereupon moved his forces and broke them at one drum.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned at the fire in panic; Su seized the moment and routed them at a single onset.

sentences.zh: 智慧將逃於海，護兒追至閩中，餘黨皆平。

translations.literal: Zhihui was about to flee to the sea; Hu'er pursued him to Minzhong and all the remaining factions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui fled toward the sea; Hu'er pursued him into Fujian and pacified the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 除泉州刺史，封襄陽縣公，食邑一千戶，賜物二千段、奴婢百人。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Quanzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang county with a fief of one thousand households, and granted two thousand lengths of goods and a hundred slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Quanzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang with a fief of one thousand households, and granted two thousand bolts of goods and a hundred slaves.

sentences.zh: 護兒招懷初附，威惠兼舉。

translations.literal: Hu'er won over those newly submitted, combining authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He won over newly submitted peoples through a blend of firmness and kindness.

sentences.zh: 璽書勞問，前後相屬。

translations.literal: Imperial letters of commendation and inquiry followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters of praise and inquiry arrived in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 時智慧餘黨盛道延阻兵為亂，護兒又討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhihui's remaining follower Sheng Daoyan blocked the roads with troops in disorder; Hu'er again attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhihui's follower Sheng Daoyan took up arms in rebellion, Hu'er suppressed him as well.

sentences.zh: 遷建州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 又與蒲山公李寬討平黟、歙逆党汪文進，進位柱國，封永寧郡公。

translations.literal: Again, with Duke of Pushan Li Kuan he attacked and pacified the rebels Wang Wenjin in Yi and She; he was advanced to pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Yongning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: With the Duke of Pushan, Li Kuan, he also suppressed the rebel Wang Wenjin in Yi and She, was promoted to pillar of state, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yongning commandery.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘉其功，使畫工圖其像以進。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised his merit and had painters depict his likeness to present at court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen commended his service and had his portrait painted and sent to court.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔追入朝，賜以宮女、寶刀、駿馬、錦彩等物，仍留長子楷為千牛備身，使護兒還職。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict recalled him to court; he was granted palace women, a precious knife, fine horses, brocades and silks, and other goods; his eldest son Kai was left as guard of the thousand oxen, and Hu'er was sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was recalled to court and rewarded with palace women, a precious sword, fine horses, and brocades; his eldest son Kai was kept at court as an imperial guard while Hu'er returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，遷瀛州刺史，以善政聞，頻見勞勉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was transferred to governor of Yingzhou, was known for good government, and was repeatedly seen and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Renshou he became governor of Yingzhou, where his good governance won repeated imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，被追入朝，百姓攀戀，累日不能出境，詣闕上書致請者，前後數百人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was recalled to court; the common people clung to him in longing and for many days he could not leave the border; those who went to the capital to submit memorials asking that he stay numbered several hundred before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was recalled to court; the people clung to him so that for days he could not cross the border, and several hundred submitted petitions begging that he remain.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「昔國步未康，卿為名將，今天下無事，又為良二千石，可謂兼美矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "In former days when the state's step was not yet secure, you were a famed general; now that all under heaven is without affairs, you are again a fine prefect—this may be called combining both excellences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "When the realm was still unsettled you were a famous general; now that the empire is at peace you prove an excellent prefect as well—you have excelled in both roles.

sentences.zh: 仍除右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed grand general of the right martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed grand general of the right martial guard.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved from the right to the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 又改上柱國為光祿大夫，徙右翊衛大將軍，進封榮國公，恩禮隆密，朝臣無比。

translations.literal: Again his title of Upper Pillar of State was changed to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, he was moved to grand general of the right wing guard, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Rong, favor and ceremony lofty and intimate, and no courtier could compare.
translations.idiomatic: He was also reassigned from Upper Pillar of State to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, transferred to grand general of the right wing guard, and ennobled as Duke of Rong; the emperor's favor toward him was unmatched among the officials at court.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，車駕幸江都，謂護兒曰：「衣錦晝游，古人所重，卿今是也。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, when the imperial carriage visited Jiangdu, the emperor said to Hu'er, "To roam by day in brocade robes is what the ancients valued, and you are that now.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daye, when the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, he told Hu'er, "The ancients prized returning home in splendor for all to see by daylight—and that is what you are doing now.

sentences.zh: 乃賜物二千段，並牛酒，令謁先人墓，宴鄉里父老。

translations.literal: He then bestowed two thousand bolts of goods, together with cattle and wine, and ordered him to visit his ancestors' tombs and feast the elders of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then gave him two thousand bolts of goods along with cattle and wine, and sent him to pay respects at his family's graves and hold a banquet for the elders of his hometown.

sentences.zh: 仍令三品已上並集其宅，酣飲盡日，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: He further ordered all officials of third rank and above to gather at his residence, and they drank deeply all day; court and countryside alike regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned every official of third rank and above to his house, where they feasted through the day—a spectacle that filled both court and country with envy.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以護兒為平壤道行軍總管，兼檢校東萊郡太守，率樓船指滄海。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, Hu'er was made commander-in-chief of the army on the Pingrang route and concurrently acting inspector of the governor of Donglai commandery, leading tower ships toward the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, Hu'er was appointed commander-in-chief of the Pingrang route and acting governor of Donglai, and led a fleet of tower ships out onto the open sea.

sentences.zh: 入自浿水，去平壤六十里，高麗主高元掃境內兵以拒之，列陣數十里。

translations.literal: Entering by the Pae River, sixty li from Pingrang, the Goguryeo ruler Gao Yuan swept up all forces within his borders to resist him and drew up battle lines for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: His force entered by the Pae River and, sixty li from Pingrang, found Goguryeo's king Gao Yuan had mobilized every soldier in the realm to meet them, arrayed in lines stretching for miles.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸懼，護兒笑謂副將周法尚及軍吏曰：「吾本謂其堅城清野以待王師，今來送死，當殄之而朝食。」

translations.literal: All the generals were afraid, but Hu'er laughed and said to his deputy Zhou Fashang and the staff officers, "I had thought they would fortify their cities and clear the countryside to await the royal army; now they come to deliver themselves to death—we should destroy them and eat breakfast.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals were alarmed, but Hu'er laughed and told his deputy Zhou Fashang and the staff, "I expected them to hold their cities and strip the countryside while they waited for our army. Instead they've come out to die—we'll wipe them out before breakfast.

sentences.zh: 高元弟建驍勇絕倫，率敢死數百人來致師。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan's younger brother Jian was peerless in fierce courage and led several hundred death-defying men to offer battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuan's brother Jian, a warrior of extraordinary daring, then led several hundred men sworn to fight to the death out to challenge them.

sentences.zh: 護兒命武賁郎將費青奴及第六子左千牛整馳斬其首，乃從兵追奔，直至城下，俘斬不可勝計，因破其郛，營於城外，以待諸軍。

translations.literal: Hu'er ordered the martial guard general Fei Qingnu and his sixth son Zheng, a left thousand-cattle guard, to ride out and cut off Jian's head; then he followed with his troops in pursuit until they reached the city walls, capturing and killing beyond counting; thus he broke through the outer suburbs, encamped outside the city, and awaited the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er sent the martial guard general Fei Qingnu and his sixth son Zheng, a palace guard officer, to ride out and behead Jian; then he pursued the fleeing enemy to the walls, taking and slaying beyond count, breached the outer suburbs, and made camp outside the city to await the other columns.

sentences.zh: 高麗晝閉城門，不敢出。

translations.literal: Goguryeo by day closed the city gates and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo forces shut the city gates by day and would not venture out.

sentences.zh: 會宇文述等眾軍皆敗，乃旋軍。

translations.literal: When it happened that the armies under Yuwen Shu and the others were all defeated, he then turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: But when Yuwen Shu and the other commanders were defeated, he withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 以功賜物五千段，以第五子弘為杜城府鷹揚郎將，以先封襄陽公賜其子整。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given five thousand bolts of goods; his fifth son Hong was made Yingyang Langjiang of Dufu prefecture, and the title of Duke of Xiangyang previously granted was bestowed on his son Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he received five thousand bolts of goods; his fifth son Hong was appointed Yingyang Langjiang of Dufu, and the earlier enfeoffment as Duke of Xiangyang was transferred to his son Zheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，又出滄海道，師次東萊，會楊玄感反，進攻洛陽，護兒聞之，召裨將周法尚等議旋軍討逆。

translations.literal: The next year he again set out by the sea route, and when the army halted at Donglai it happened that Yang Xuangan rebelled and advanced to attack Luoyang; on hearing this, Hu'er summoned his subordinate generals Zhou Fashang and the others to discuss turning the army back to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again took the sea route, but while his army was at Donglai, Yang Xuangan rebelled and marched on Luoyang. Hearing this, Hu'er called his subordinates, including Zhou Fashang, to discuss turning back to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 法尚等咸以無敕，不宜擅還，再三固執不從。

translations.literal: Fashang and the others all held that without an imperial order they should not return on their own authority, and repeatedly stood firm and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang and the others insisted that without an imperial order they had no right to withdraw on their own, and repeatedly refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 護兒厲聲曰：「洛陽被圍，心腹之疾。

translations.literal: Hu'er said in a harsh voice, "Luoyang is besieged—that is a disease of the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er said sharply, "Luoyang is under siege—that is a mortal wound at the empire's heart.

sentences.zh: 高麗逆命，猶疥癬耳。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's defiance of orders is still only scabies and tetter.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's rebellion is nothing more than a skin rash by comparison.

sentences.zh: 公家之事，知無不為，專擅在吾，當不關諸人也。

translations.literal: In affairs of the public house, knowing what must be done one does it; exclusive authority rests with me, and it should not concern the rest of you.
translations.idiomatic: In the service of the state, one must act whenever action is needed. The decision is mine alone, and none of you need answer for it.

sentences.zh: 有沮議者，軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Whoever discourages the plan shall be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who tries to talk us out of it will face the full penalty of military law.

sentences.zh: 即日回軍。

translations.literal: That same day he turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he marched his army back.

sentences.zh: 令子弘及整馳驛奏聞。

translations.literal: He ordered his sons Hong and Zheng to ride post-horses and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons Hong and Zheng ahead by relay horse to inform the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝見弘等甚悅，曰：「汝父擅赴國難，乃誠臣也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor saw Hong and the others he was greatly pleased and said, "Your father on his own authority went to meet the state's peril—he is a true minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted to see Hong and the others and said, "Your father took it upon himself to rush to the empire's aid—he is a loyal minister indeed.

sentences.zh: 授弘通議大夫，整公路府鷹揚即將，乃降璽書於護兒曰：「公旋師之時，是朕敕公之日，君臣授弘意合，遠同符契。

translations.literal: He appointed Hong General Consultant and Zheng Yingyang Commander of the Highway Office, then issued an imperial letter to Hu'er saying, "When you turned the army was the day I ordered you; ruler and minister, in appointing Hong, were of one mind, distant yet like matching tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: He made Hong a General Consultant and Zheng a Yingyang commander of the Highway Office, then sent Hu'er an imperial letter saying, "The day you turned your army was the day I would have ordered you to do so. In rewarding Hong, ruler and subject were of one mind—as though our intentions had matched from afar.

sentences.zh: 梟此元惡，期在不遙，勒名太常，非公而誰也！」

translations.literal: To behead this arch villain—the time is not far off; to inscribe a name in the Grand Master of Ceremonies' records—if not you, then who!"
translations.idiomatic: The beheading of this chief rebel is near at hand, and when your name is entered in the temple records of honor, who but you should receive it!"

sentences.zh: 於是護兒與宇文述破玄感於閿鄉，斬平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hu'er together with Yuwen Shu defeated Xuangan at Wenxiang and beheaded him, ending the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er and Yuwen Shu then routed Xuangan at Wenxiang and put the rebellion down by executing him.

sentences.zh: 還，加開府儀同三司，賜物五千段、黃金千兩、奴婢百人，贈父法敏東陽郡太守、永甯縣公。

translations.literal: On his return he was given the rank of honorary grand master with golden insignia of the first order, granted five thousand bolts of goods, a thousand taels of gold, and a hundred male and female servants, and his father Famin was posthumously made governor of Dongyang commandery and Duke of Yongning county.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was promoted to honorary grand master with golden insignia of the first order and given five thousand bolts of goods, a thousand taels of gold, and a hundred servants; his father Famin was posthumously honored as governor of Dongyang and Duke of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又率師渡海，破高麗奢卑等二城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again led an army across the sea and captured the two Goguryeo cities of She and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again led troops across the sea and took two Goguryeo cities, She and Bei.

sentences.zh: 高麗舉國來戰，護兒大破之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo mustered the whole state to give battle, and Hu'er routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo mobilized the entire kingdom to fight, Hu'er inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 將趣平壤，高元震懼，使執叛臣斛斯政詣遼東城下請降。

translations.literal: As he was about to press on to Pingrang, Gao Yuan was shaken with fear and had the rebel minister Husi Zheng seized and sent to the foot of Liaodong city to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As he was advancing on Pingrang, Gao Yuan, terrified, had the renegade minister Husi Zheng arrested and brought to the walls of Liaodong to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，詔護兒旋軍。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it and ordered Hu'er to turn the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted and ordered Hu'er to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 護兒集眾軍謂曰：「三度出兵，未能平賊。

translations.literal: Hu'er gathered the armies and said, "Three times we have sent out troops and failed to pacify the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er assembled the commanders and said, "We have marched against them three times and still have not crushed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 此還也，不可重來。

translations.literal: If we return this time, we cannot come again.
translations.idiomatic: If we turn back now, we may never get another chance.

sentences.zh: 今高麗困弊，野無青草，以我眾戰，不日克之。

translations.literal: Now Goguryeo is exhausted and distressed, the wilds have no green grass; with our massed troops in battle, we will take them in no many days.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo is now exhausted and the countryside is stripped bare; with our numbers we can finish them off in a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 吾欲進兵，徑圍平壤，取其偽主，獻捷而歸也。」

translations.literal: I wish to advance the army, go straight to besiege Pingrang, take their false ruler, and return presenting victory.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to press on, lay siege to Pingrang at once, seize their pretender king, and return in triumph.

sentences.zh: 於是拜表請行，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting to proceed and refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne asking to advance and refused to obey the recall order.

sentences.zh: 長史崔君肅固爭之，以為不可。

translations.literal: Chief administrator Cui Junsu firmly disputed it, holding that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: His chief administrator Cui Junsu argued strenuously against the plan.

sentences.zh: 護兒曰：「賊勢破矣。

translations.literal: Hu'er said, "The enemy's strength is already broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er replied, "The enemy is already beaten.

sentences.zh: 吾在閫外，事合專決，甯征得高元，還而獲譴，舍此成功，所不能矣。」

translations.literal: I am outside the gate; affairs should be decided exclusively by me. I would rather capture Gao Yuan and return to face censure than abandon this success—I cannot do that.
translations.idiomatic: I hold independent command beyond the capital, and the decision is mine. I would rather capture Gao Yuan and face punishment afterward than throw away victory now—that I cannot do.

sentences.zh: 君肅告眾曰：「若從元帥，違拒詔書，必當奏聞。」

translations.literal: Junsu told the assembly, "If we follow the commander-in-chief and defy and refuse the edict, this must be reported to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Junsu then told the officers, "If we follow the commander and disobey the imperial order, I will have no choice but to report it to the throne."

sentences.zh: 諸將懼，乃同勸還師，方始奉詔。

translations.literal: The generals were afraid, and together urged withdrawal; only then did he obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the generals united in urging a withdrawal, and only then did he obey the order.

sentences.zh: 及帝於雁門為突厥所圍，將選精騎潰圍而出，護兒及樊子蓋並固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: When the emperor at Yanmen was besieged by the Turks and was about to choose elite cavalry to break through the encirclement and escape, Hu'er and Fan Zigai both firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor was trapped by Turks at Yanmen and prepared to break out with a picked cavalry force, Hu'er and Fan Zigai both strongly dissuaded him, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，駕幸江都，護兒諫曰：「自皇家受命，將四十年，薄賦輕徭，戶口滋殖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the imperial carriage visited Jiangdu, Hu'er remonstrated, saying, "Since the imperial house received the mandate, it will soon be forty years; light taxes and easy corvée labor have made households multiply and flourish.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when the emperor visited Jiangdu, Hu'er admonished him: "Since the dynasty received Heaven's mandate, nearly forty years have passed of light taxes and easy labor, and the population has grown steadily.

sentences.zh: 陛下以高麗逆命，稍興軍旅，百姓無知，易為咨怨，在外群盜，往往聚結，車駕遊幸，深恐非宜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because Goguryeo defied orders, has somewhat raised armies and camps; the common people, without understanding, are easily moved to complaint and resentment; outside, bands of robbers often gather and join together; the imperial carriage's pleasure tour is deeply to be feared as unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's campaigns against rebellious Goguryeo have strained the people, who easily turn to complaint; bandits are gathering everywhere in the provinces; and I greatly fear that an imperial tour is ill advised at such a time.

sentences.zh: 伏願駐駕洛陽，與時休息，出師命將，掃清群醜，上稟聖算，指日克除。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty would halt the carriage at Luoyang and rest with the times, send out armies and appoint generals to sweep clear the mass of villains, obeying above the sage calculations, and remove them within a counted number of days.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remain at Luoyang and let the realm recover, dispatch generals to sweep away the rebels, and trust that your wise strategy will destroy them in short order.

sentences.zh: 陛下今幸江都，是臣衣錦之地，臣荷恩深重，不敢專為身謀。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty now visits Jiangdu, which is the place where this subject returns in brocade robes; this subject bears deep grace and does not dare plan only for himself.
translations.idiomatic: I know Jiangdu is my own homeland, where I might glory in your visit, but the favor I owe the throne is too great for me to speak from private interest alone.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，厲色而起，數日不得見。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, his face grew stern and he rose; for several days Hu'er was not granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened and he walked out; for days afterward Hu'er was denied audience.

sentences.zh: 後怒解，方被引入，謂曰：「公意乃爾，朕復何望！」

translations.literal: Later, when his anger subsided, Hu'er was at last brought in, and the emperor said, "Your intent is thus—what more can I hope for!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's anger finally cooled, Hu'er was summoned again and told, "So that is your view of things—what more can I expect from you!

sentences.zh: 護兒因不敢言。

translations.literal: Hu'er therefore did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er said no more.

sentences.zh: 尋代宇文述為左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Yuwen Shu as grand general of the left wing guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he succeeded Yuwen Shu as grand general of the left wing guard.

sentences.zh: 及宇文化及構逆，深忌之。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji plotted rebellion, he deeply feared Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji plotted treason, he regarded Hu'er with deep suspicion.

sentences.zh: 是日旦將朝，見執。

translations.literal: That morning, as he was about to attend court, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: That morning, on his way to court, he was seized.

sentences.zh: 護兒曰：「陛下今何在？」

translations.literal: Hu'er said, "Where is Your Majesty now?
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er asked, "Where is His Majesty now?

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「今被執矣。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "He is now seized."
translations.idiomatic: Those around him replied, "He has already been taken captive."

sentences.zh: 護兒歎曰：「吾備位大臣，荷國重任，不能肅清凶逆，遂令王室至此，抱恨泉壤，知復何言！」

translations.literal: Hu'er sighed and said, "I occupy a minister's place and bear the state's heavy responsibility, yet could not purge the violent rebels, and so allowed the royal house to come to this; embracing resentment in the yellow springs, what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er sighed and said, "I stand among the great ministers charged with the fate of the state, yet failed to destroy these traitors and allowed the dynasty to come to this pass. I shall carry this shame to my grave—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 乃遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then put to death.

sentences.zh: 護兒重然諾，敦交契，廉於財利，不事產業。

translations.literal: Hu'er valued keeping his word, was earnest in friendship and bonds, was incorrupt regarding wealth and profit, and did not pursue estates and property.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er was a man of his word, loyal in friendship, scrupulous about money, and indifferent to building up an estate.

sentences.zh: 至於行軍用兵，特多謀算，每覽兵法，曰：「此亦豈異人意也！」

translations.literal: As for marching armies and using troops, he was especially rich in plans and calculations; whenever he read military classics he would say, "This too is surely no different from ordinary human understanding!
translations.idiomatic: In campaigning and command he was unusually resourceful, and whenever he read the military classics he would remark, "This is only what any sensible man would think!

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒，部分嚴明，故咸得其死力。

translations.literal: He was good at comforting soldiers, his divisions and arrangements were strict and clear, and therefore all gave him their utmost strength even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his soldiers well and kept discipline strict, and so they fought for him with their lives.

sentences.zh: 子十二人，楷通議大夫，弘金紫光祿大夫，整左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons: Kai was General Consultant, Hong was Grand Master with the Purple-Gold Seal and Splendid Happiness, and Zheng was Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons. Kai became a General Consultant, Hong a Grand Master with the Purple-Gold Seal, and Zheng a Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 整尤驍勇，善撫禦，討擊群盜，所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Zheng was especially fierce and brave, good at comforting and controlling troops, and in attacking and striking bandit bands wherever he went he was always victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was especially bold in battle, skilled at handling troops, and undefeated in his campaigns against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 諸賊歌曰：「長白山頭百戰場，十十五五把長槍。

translations.literal: The bandits sang, "On the head of Mount Changbai is a hundred-battle field; by tens and fifteens they grasp long spears.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had a song: "On Mount Changbai's heights the battles rage, and spearmen stand in ranks of ten and fifteen.

sentences.zh: 不畏官軍千萬眾，只怕榮公第六郎。」

translations.literal: They do not fear millions in the official army, but only fear the Duke of Rong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: We fear not the imperial armies in their millions—we fear only the Duke of Rong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 至是，並遇禍，子侄死者十人，唯少子恆、濟二人免。

translations.literal: At this time they all met disaster; among sons and nephews ten died, and only the younger sons Heng and Ji escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup came, they all perished: ten of his sons and nephews were killed, and only his youngest sons Heng and Ji survived.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋，字華宗，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai, styled Huazong, was a man of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai, courtesy name Huazong, came from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖道則，梁越州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daozhe was governor of Yuezhou under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daozhe had served as governor of Yuezhou under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父儒，侯景之亂奔齊，位仁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ru, during Hou Jing's rebellion fled to Qi and held the post of governor of Renzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru fled to Northern Qi during Hou Jing's rebellion and rose to governor of Renzhou.

sentences.zh: 子蓋仕齊，位東海北陳二郡太守、員外散騎常侍，封富陽侯。

translations.literal: Zigai served Qi, held the posts of governor of the two commanderies Donghai and Beichen, and was an extra attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai served Northern Qi as governor of Donghai and Beichen, as an attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授儀同三司、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was granted the rank of honorary grand master of the third order and made governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he was made an honorary grand master of the third order and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，以儀同領鄉兵，後除樅陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he served as honorary grand master commanding district troops, and later was removed to be governor of Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he commanded local militia with the rank of honorary grand master and later became governor of Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以功加上開府，改封上蔡縣伯，曆辰、嵩、齊三州刺史，轉循州總管，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, for merit he was given the additional rank of honorary grand master with the first order, his enfeoffment was changed to Count of Shangcai county, he served successively as governor of the three provinces Chen, Song, and Qi, was transferred to area commander of Xunzhou, and was permitted to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he was promoted to honorary grand master with the first order and made Count of Shangcai; he then served as governor of Chen, Song, and Qi in turn before becoming area commander of Xunzhou with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 十八年，入朝，奏嶺南地圖，賜以良馬雜物，加統四州，令還任所，遣光祿少卿柳謇之餞於灞上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered court, presented a map of Lingnan, was given fine horses and assorted goods, was given charge over four additional provinces, was ordered to return to his post, and the vice director of the Directorate for Imperial Regalia Liu Jianzhi was sent to give him a farewell at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he came to court and presented a map of Lingnan; the emperor rewarded him with fine horses and other gifts, added four provinces to his command, and sent him back to his post after Liu Jianzhi, vice director of the Directorate for Imperial Regalia, saw him off at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉涼州刺史，改授銀青光祿大夫、武威太守，以善政聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was transferred to governor of Liangzhou, reassigned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal and governor of Wuwei, and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he became governor of Liangzhou and then Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal and governor of Wuwei, where his good governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，入朝，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he entered court and was given the additional title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Purple-Gold Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he came to court and was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Purple-Gold Seal.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西巡，將入吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage toured west and was about to enter Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor toured the west and prepared to enter Tuyuhun territory.

sentences.zh: 子蓋以彼多瘴氣，獻青木香，以禦霧露。

translations.literal: Zigai, because that region had much miasmic vapor, presented agalloch incense to ward off mist and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region was thick with miasma, Zigai presented agalloch wood incense to protect the emperor from damp and fog.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，謂曰：「人道公清，定如此不？

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he said to him, "People say you are incorrupt—are you really so?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he asked him, "People call you incorruptible—is that really true?

sentences.zh: 「子蓋謝曰：「臣安敢清，止是小心不敢納賄耳。」

translations.literal: Zigai thanked him and said, "How would your subject dare claim to be incorrupt? I am only careful and do not dare accept bribes, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Zigai replied humbly, "How could I claim to be incorruptible? I am merely cautious and refuse to take bribes, that is all."

sentences.zh: 於是賜之口味百餘斛，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given more than a hundred hu of delicacies and promoted to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then gave him more than a hundred hu of delicacies and promoted him to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子蓋曰：「願奉丹陛。」

translations.literal: Zigai said, "I wish to serve at the cinnabar steps."
translations.idiomatic: Zigai said, "I would rather serve at Your Majesty's side in court."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公侍朕則一人而已，委以西方，則萬人之敵，宜識此心。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When you attend Us you are but one man, but entrusted with the west you are a match for ten thousand men—you should recognize this heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "At court you are one man among many, but entrusted with the west you are worth ten thousand soldiers—remember that this is how I regard you."

sentences.zh: 六年，帝避暑隴川宮，又云欲幸河西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor summered at Longchuan Palace and again said he wished to visit Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor took the summer heat at Longchuan Palace and again spoke of touring Hexi.

sentences.zh: 子蓋傾望鑾輿，願巡郡境。

translations.literal: Zigai looked eagerly toward the imperial carriage and hoped the tour would pass through his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai watched eagerly for the imperial progress, hoping the emperor would visit his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，下詔慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this and issued an edict to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the emperor issued an edict to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，朝于江都宮，帝謂曰：「富貴不還故鄉，真衣繡夜行耳。」

translations.literal: That year, when he attended court at Jiangdu Palace, the emperor said, "Wealth and honor without returning to one's old home is truly like wearing brocade and walking at night."
translations.idiomatic: That year, when he came to court at Jiangdu, the emperor told him, "To gain wealth and rank yet never return home is like wearing brocade in the dark—no one sees it."

sentences.zh: 因敕廬江郡設三千人會，賜米麥六千石，使謁墳墓，宴故老，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Lujiang commandery to set up a gathering of three thousand people, granted six thousand shi of rice and wheat, and had him visit the tombs and feast the old friends of former days; at the time this was regarded as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a gathering of three thousand people in Lujiang, gave six thousand shi of grain, and sent Zigai to visit his family's graves and entertain the elders of his hometown—a spectacle that filled the age with envy.

sentences.zh: 還除戶部尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時處羅可汗及高昌王款塞，復以子蓋檢校武威太守，應接二蕃。

translations.literal: At that time Chulu Qaghan and the king of Gaochang came to the border with sincerity; Zigai was again made acting governor of Wuwei to receive and respond to the two frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: When Chulu Qaghan and the king of Gaochang submitted at the frontier, Zigai was again appointed acting governor of Wuwei to receive them.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，攝左武衛將軍，出長岑道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he served as acting general of the left martial guard and set out by the Changcen route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he served as acting general of the left martial guard and marched by the Changcen route.

sentences.zh: 後以宿衛不行。

translations.literal: Later, because of palace guard duty, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was kept from going because of his duties in palace guard service.

sentences.zh: 加左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 其年，帝還東都，使子蓋涿郡留守。

translations.literal: That year, when the emperor returned to the eastern capital, he made Zigai remain to hold Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the emperor returned to the eastern capital, he left Zigai behind as military governor of Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，駕復幸遼東，命子蓋東都留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the imperial carriage again visited Liaodong, he ordered Zigai to remain and hold the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the emperor again marched on Liaodong, he appointed Zigai to hold Luoyang as military governor.

sentences.zh: 屬楊玄感作逆，逼城，子蓋遣河南贊務裴弘策逆擊之，反為所敗，遂斬弘策以徇。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan rebelled and pressed the city; Zigai sent Henan assistant prefect Pei Hongce to meet and strike him, but was in turn defeated by him, and so executed Hongce to display as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and besieged the city, Zigai sent Henan assistant prefect Pei Hongce to attack him; Pei was defeated, and Zigai had him executed as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒楊汪小不恭，子蓋又將斬之。

translations.literal: National University libationer Yang Wang showed a slight lack of respect, and Zigai was again about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When National University libationer Yang Wang showed a slight lack of respect, Zigai was ready to execute him as well.

sentences.zh: 汪拜謝，頓首流血，久乃釋免。

translations.literal: Wang bowed in thanks, knocked his head until blood flowed, and only after a long time was he released and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang bowed in apology and kowtowed until his forehead bled; only after a long time did Zigai spare him.

sentences.zh: 於是三軍莫不戰慄，將吏無敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon throughout the three armies none did not tremble in battle-fear, and officers and clerks did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: After that the entire army trembled with fear, and officers and clerks dared not even meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 玄感每盡銳攻城，子蓋徐設備禦，至輒摧破。

translations.literal: Each time Xuangan exhausted his elite forces in attacking the city, Zigai slowly set defenses and preparations, and whenever he arrived he shattered and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xuangan threw his best troops against the walls, Zigai methodically organized the defenses and repulsed every assault.

sentences.zh: 會來護等救至，玄感乃解去。

translations.literal: When it happened that Lai Hu and the others arrived with relief, Xuangan then lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Hu'er and the other relief forces arrived, Xuangan broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 子蓋凡所誅殺萬人。

translations.literal: In all, those whom Zigai executed and killed numbered ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In all, Zigai had ten thousand people executed.

sentences.zh: 又檢校河南內史。

translations.literal: He was again made acting Henan interior secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed acting Henan interior secretary.

sentences.zh: 車駕至高陽，追詣行在所，帝勞之，以比蕭何、寇恂，加光祿大夫，封建安侯，賜女樂五十人。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Gaoyang; he pursued to the traveling palace; the emperor comforted him, compared him to Xiao He and Kou Xun, added Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jian'an, and bestowed fifty female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Gaoyang, Zigai hurried to the traveling palace. The emperor praised him, likening him to Xiao He and Kou Xun, promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jian'an, and granted him fifty female musicians.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「朕遣越王留守東都，示以皇枝磐石，社稷大事，終以委公。

translations.literal: He said to him: "I have dispatched the Prince of Yue to remain and guard the eastern capital, showing the imperial branches as bedrock; the great affairs of state and altars I ultimately entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "I have left the Prince of Yue at Luoyang to show that the imperial house rests on bedrock. The weight of the realm I ultimately place in your hands.

sentences.zh: 特宜持重，戈甲五百人而後出，此勇夫重閉之義。

translations.literal: It is especially fitting to hold a grave demeanor: five hundred armed men, and only then go out — this is the principle of a brave man heavily guarded.
translations.idiomatic: You must conduct yourself with utmost gravity — do not leave your residence without five hundred armed men at your side. That is how a man of courage keeps himself sealed and secure.

sentences.zh: 無賴不軌者，便誅鋤之，凡可施行，無勞形跡。

translations.literal: Ruffians and lawless men — execute and root them out at once; whatever can be done, do not trouble over appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Cut down ruffians and rebels on the spot. Do whatever must be done, and do not fuss over formalities.

sentences.zh: 今為公別造玉麟符，以代銅獸。」

translations.literal: Now for you I have specially made a jade unicorn tally to replace the bronze beast.
translations.idiomatic: I have had a new jade unicorn tally made for you, to replace the old bronze one.

sentences.zh: 又指越、代二王曰：「今以二孫委公與衛文升耳。

translations.literal: He also pointed to the two princes of Yue and Dai and said: "Now I entrust these two grandsons to you and Wei Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then indicated the princes of Yue and Dai and said, "I now leave these two grandsons in your care, and in Wei Wensheng's as well.

sentences.zh: 宜選貞良宿德有方幅者教習之。」

translations.literal: You should select upright and good men of long-standing virtue and proper measure to teach and instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: Choose upright, seasoned men of proven character to train and guide them."

sentences.zh: 於是賜以良田、甲第。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed fine fields and a first-rank mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him rich farmland and a grand mansion.

sentences.zh: 十年，駕還東都，帝謂子蓋曰：「玄感之反，神明故以彰公赤心耳。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the imperial progress returned to the eastern capital, the emperor said to Zigai: "Xuangan's rebellion — the spirits therefore revealed your loyal heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the emperor returned to Luoyang, he told Zigai, "Heaven itself used Xuangan's rebellion to reveal your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 析珪進爵，宜有令謨。」

translations.literal: Having divided the jade tablet and advanced in rank, you ought to have excellent counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Having been rewarded with rank and a fief, you ought to offer worthy counsel.

sentences.zh: 是日進爵為濟公，言其功濟天下，特為立名，無此郡國也。

translations.literal: That day his rank was advanced to Duke of Ji, meaning his merit aided the realm; the title was specially created — there is no such commandery or state.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was raised to Duke of Ji — "Ji" meaning that his service had aided the realm. The title was invented for him alone; no such fief existed.

sentences.zh: 後與蘇威、宇文述陪宴積翠池，帝親以金杯屬子蓋酒，曰：「良算嘉謀，俟公後動，即以此杯賜公，用為永年之瑞。」

translations.literal: Later, together with Su Wei and Yuwen Shu, he attended a banquet at Emerald Pool; the emperor personally entrusted wine to Zigai with a golden cup and said: "Good calculations and fine plans — await your later actions; then with this cup I shall gift you, using it as an omen of eternal years."
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet at Emerald Pool with Su Wei and Yuwen Shu, the emperor personally filled a golden cup for Zigai and said, "When your wise plans bear fruit in days to come, I shall give you this cup as a token of long life."

sentences.zh: 十一年，從駕至雁門，為突厥所圍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he followed the imperial progress to Yanmen and was surrounded by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor to Yanmen, where they were besieged by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝欲選精騎潰圍出，子蓋及來護諫，因垂泣：「願暫停遼東之役，以慰眾望。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to select elite cavalry to break the encirclement and escape; Zigai and Lai Hu admonished him, then shedding tears said: "I wish temporarily to halt the Liaodong campaign, to comfort the hopes of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to break out with a picked cavalry force, but Zigai and Lai Hu'er dissuaded him, weeping as they spoke: "Suspend the Liaodong campaign for now, and give the people what they hope for.

sentences.zh: 聖躬親出慰撫，厚為勳格，人心自奮，不足為憂。」

translations.literal: Let the sacred person himself go out to comfort and soothe; set generous standards of merit; the hearts of men will themselves be roused — this is not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty goes out in person to rally the troops and sets generous rewards for merit, the men will fight of their own accord. There is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，後援兵至，虜乃去。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; later relief troops arrived, and the barbarians then departed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted their advice. When reinforcements arrived, the Turks withdrew.

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威追論勳格太重，宜在斟酌。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Su Wei pursued the argument that the standards of merit were too heavy and ought to be weighed with deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Su Wei later argued that the promised rewards had been too lavish and should be scaled back.

sentences.zh: 子蓋執奏不宜失信。

translations.literal: Zigai firmly memorialized that it was inappropriate to break faith.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai insisted in a memorial that the emperor must not go back on his word.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公欲收物情邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you wish to win popular sentiment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Are you trying to win the people's favor?

sentences.zh: 子蓋默然不敢對。

translations.literal: Zigai was silent and did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai fell silent and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 從駕還東都。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial progress back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Luoyang with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時絳郡賊敬槃陀、柴保昌等阻兵數萬，汾、晉苦之，詔子蓋進討。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits Jing Panto, Chai Baochang, and others of Jiang commandery held armed forces numbering tens of thousands; Fen and Jin suffered from them; an edict ordered Zigai to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels Jing Panto, Chai Baochang, and others in Jiang commandery mustered tens of thousands of men, ravaging Fen and Jin. An edict ordered Zigai to march against them.

sentences.zh: 時人物殷阜，子蓋善惡無所分別，汾水北村塢盡焚之。

translations.literal: At the time people and goods were abundant; Zigai made no distinction between good and evil, and burned all the north-of-Fen River village stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The region was populous and prosperous, yet Zigai made no distinction between loyal villagers and rebels and burned every stockade north of the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 百姓大駭，相率為盜。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly terrified and joined together as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people were terrified and turned to banditry in droves.

sentences.zh: 其歸首者，無少長悉坑之。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered — regardless of age, all were executed in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrendered, young and old alike, were buried alive in mass graves.

sentences.zh: 擁數萬眾，經年不能破賊，詔徵還，又將兵擊宜陽賊，以疾停，卒于東京。

translations.literal: Commanding tens of thousands, for a year he could not break the bandits; an edict recalled him; he was again about to lead troops against the Yiyang bandits, but illness stopped him, and he died at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though he commanded tens of thousands, he failed to crush the rebels for a full year and was recalled. He was preparing to lead troops against the Yiyang rebels when illness stopped him, and he died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 上悲傷者久之，顧黃門侍郎裴矩曰：「子蓋臨終何語？」

translations.literal: The emperor grieved for a long time, turned to Household Undersecretary Pei Ju, and said: "What words did Zigai speak at his end?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned for a long time, then turned to Household Undersecretary Pei Ju and asked, "What were Zigai's last words?

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「子蓋病篤，深恨雁門之恥。」

translations.literal: Ju said: "Zigai's illness was grave; he deeply regretted the disgrace at Yanmen."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju replied, "Near death, Zigai bitterly lamented the humiliation at Yanmen."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之歎息，令百官就吊，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰景。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and sighed; he ordered the hundred officials to go offer condolences; posthumously granted Opening the Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed at this and ordered the officials to attend the funeral. Zigai was posthumously granted the rank of Opening the Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 會葬萬餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand people gathered for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand people attended his funeral.

sentences.zh: 武威人吏聞其死，莫不嗟痛，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Officials and clerks of Wuwei, hearing of his death, none did not sigh in grief; they erected steles praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials and clerks of Wuwei heard of his death, all mourned him and erected steles in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 子蓋無他權略，在軍持重，未嘗負敗，蒞官明察，下莫敢欺。

translations.literal: Zigai had no other schemes of power; in the army he held a grave demeanor and never suffered defeat; when attending office he was bright in scrutiny, and subordinates did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai had no gift for intrigue, but in the field he was steady and never knew defeat. As an administrator he was sharp-eyed, and none beneath him dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 嚴酷少恩，果於殺戮，臨終之日，見斷頭鬼前後重遝，為之厲云。
