translations.literal: He was severe and cruel, sparing little grace, and decisive in killing; on the day of his death he saw severed-head ghosts overlapping before and behind, and they wailed fiercely at him.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh and merciless, swift to kill. On his last day he saw severed-head ghosts crowding before and behind him, shrieking at him in fury.

sentences.zh: 周羅碶，字公佈，九江尋陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Luohou, courtesy name Gongbu, was a man of Xunyang in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Luohou, whose courtesy name was Gongbu, came from Xunyang in Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 父法皓，仕梁，至南康內史、臨蒸縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Fahao served Liang, reaching the posts of Interior Secretary of Nankang and Marquis of Linzheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fahao served the Liang dynasty, rising to Interior Secretary of Nankang and Marquis of Linzheng county.

sentences.zh: 羅碶年十五，善騎射，好鷹狗，任俠放蕩，收聚亡命，陰習兵書。

translations.literal: At fifteen Luohou was skilled at mounted archery, fond of hawks and dogs, chivalrous and unrestrained, gathered fugitives, and secretly studied military texts.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Luohou was already an expert horseman and archer, devoted to hawking and hunting. Reckless and swaggering, he gathered fugitives and studied military texts in secret.

sentences.zh: 從祖景彥誡之曰：「吾世恭謹，汝獨放縱，若不喪身，必將滅吾族。」

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Jing Yan admonished him, saying: "Our clan for generations has been reverent and careful; you alone are unrestrained — if you do not lose your life, you will surely destroy our clan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Jing Yan warned him, "Our family has always been dutiful and restrained. You alone run wild. If you do not destroy yourself, you will destroy us all.

sentences.zh: 羅碶終不改。

translations.literal: Luohou ultimately did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou never changed his ways.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，為句容令。

translations.literal: He served Chen and became magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Chen and became magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 後從大都督吳明徹與齊師戰于江陽，為流矢中左目。

translations.literal: Later he followed Grand Commander Wu Mingche in battle with the Qi army at Jiangyang and was struck in the left eye by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving under Grand Commander Wu Mingche, he fought the Qi at Jiangyang and took a stray arrow in his left eye.

sentences.zh: 齊師之圍明徹於宿預也，諸軍相顧，莫有鬥心。

translations.literal: When the Qi army besieged Mingche at Suyu, the various armies looked at one another — none had the will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi besieged Mingche at Suyu, the allied armies lost heart and none would fight.

sentences.zh: 羅碶躍馬突進，莫不披靡。

translations.literal: Luohou leaped on his horse and charged forward; none did not scatter before him.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou spurred his horse forward in a charge, and the enemy lines broke before him.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿蕭摩訶副之，斬首不可勝計。

translations.literal: Minister of the Imperial Stud Xiao Mohe assisted him, and heads cut off could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Imperial Stud Xiao Mohe joined the attack, and the enemy dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 進師徐州，與周將梁士彥戰于彭城，摩訶臨陣墮馬，羅碶進救之於重圍之內，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Advancing the army to Xuzhou, he fought Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Pengcheng; Mohe fell from his horse on the battlefield, and Luohou advanced to rescue him within the heavy encirclement — his bravery topped the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the army advanced on Xuzhou and fought Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Pengcheng, Mohe was unhorsed in the thick of battle. Luohou fought his way through the encirclement to save him, and his courage outshone every man in the army.

sentences.zh: 明徹之敗，羅碶全眾而歸。

translations.literal: When Mingche was defeated, Luohou brought the whole force back safely.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingche's army was defeated, Luohou brought his troops home intact.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功除右軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later, by military merit, he was appointed General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: For his military service he was appointed General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 封始安縣伯，總檢校揚州中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Shian county and made general inspector of all military affairs within and without Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Shian county and put in overall command of military affairs in and around Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賜金銀三千兩，盡散之將士，分賞驍雄。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand liang of gold and silver, entirely distributed to officers and soldiers, with rewards divided among the fiercest champions.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three thousand liang of gold and silver, which he gave away entirely to his officers and men, reserving special rewards for the bravest.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝深歎美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 出為晉陵太守，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Jinling and was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Jinling and promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 後除使持節、都督豫章十郡諸軍事、豫章內史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Director of Military Affairs for the ten commanderies of Yuzhang, and Interior Secretary of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, military governor of the ten Yuzhang commanderies, and Interior Secretary of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 獄訟庭決，不關吏手，人懷其惠，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Prison cases and lawsuits he decided in the court hall, not passing through clerks' hands; the people cherished his grace, and steles were erected praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He settled lawsuits in open court without leaving matters to clerks. The people loved him for it, and steles were raised in his honor.

sentences.zh: 至德中，除持節、都督南州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the Zhide period he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Director of Military Affairs of Nanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and military governor of Nanzhou.

sentences.zh: 江州司馬吳世興密奏羅碶甚得人心，擁眾嶺表，意在難測。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou Vice Commander Wu Shixing secretly memorialized that Luohou greatly won people's hearts, commanded troops in the Ling region, and his intentions were hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou Vice Commander Wu Shixing secretly reported that Luohou had won the people's hearts, commanded a large force in the Ling region, and might harbor designs that could not be read.

sentences.zh: 陳主惑焉。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler was perplexed by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor was troubled by the report.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶、魯廣達等保明之。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe, Lu Guangda, and others vouched for him and cleared his name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe, Lu Guangda, and others spoke up in his defense.

sentences.zh: 外有知者，或勸其反，羅碶拒絕之。

translations.literal: Outsiders who knew of this sometimes urged him to rebel, but Luohou refused.
translations.idiomatic: Some who knew of the suspicion urged him to rebel, but Luohou refused.

sentences.zh: 還除太子左術率，信任愈重，時參宴席。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Left Tactical Commander of the Heir Apparent; trust in him grew heavier, and he often participated in banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made Left Tactical Commander of the Heir Apparent. The emperor trusted him ever more deeply and often had him at court banquets.

sentences.zh: 陳主曰：「周左率武將，詩每前成，文士何為後也？」

translations.literal: The Chen ruler said: "Left Commander Zhou is a military man — his poems are always finished first; why are the literary men behind?
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor said, "Commander Zhou is a soldier, yet his poems are always finished first. Why do the literati lag behind?

sentences.zh: 都官尚書孔范曰：「周羅碶執筆制詩，還如上馬入陣，不在人後。」

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Revenue Kong Fan said: "When Zhou Luohou takes brush to compose poems, it is still like mounting a horse and entering battle — he is not behind others."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Revenue Kong Fan replied, "When Zhou Luohou takes up the brush, he is no slower than when he mounts a horse and enters battle. He never falls behind."

sentences.zh: 自是益見親禮。

translations.literal: From this he was even more treated with intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After that he enjoyed even greater favor at court.

sentences.zh: 及隋伐陳，羅碶都督巴峽緣江諸軍事以拒秦王俊。

translations.literal: When Sui attacked Chen, Luohou was made Director of Military Affairs along the Ba and Xia gorges on the Yangzi to resist Qin commandery's Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui invaded Chen, Luohou was put in command of the Yangzi garrison from the Ba and Xia gorges to resist Wang Jun of Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 及陳主被禽，上江猶不下，晉王廣遣陳主手書命之。

translations.literal: When the Chen ruler was captured, the upper Yangzi still did not submit; the Prince of Jin Guang sent the Chen ruler's personal letter ordering him.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Chen emperor was taken, the upper Yangzi still held out. Prince Guang sent an order in the captive emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 羅碶與諸將大臨三日，放兵士散，然後乃降。

translations.literal: Luohou and the generals wept greatly for three days, released the soldiers to disperse, and only then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou and his officers mourned for three days, dismissed their troops, and only then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 文帝慰喻之，許以富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen comforted and instructed him and promised wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen comforted him and promised him wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 羅碶垂泣對曰：「本朝淪亡，臣無節可紀。

translations.literal: Luohou, weeping, replied: "Our dynasty is lost in ruin; your servant has no integrity worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou answered through tears, "My dynasty is destroyed. I have no loyal deed worth remembering.

sentences.zh: 陛下所賜，獲全為幸，富貴榮祿，非臣所望。」

translations.literal: What Your Majesty has granted — to be preserved whole is already fortune; wealth, honor, and emoluments are not what your servant desires.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty has spared my life is blessing enough. Wealth and glory are not what I seek.

sentences.zh: 帝甚器之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼謂曰：「聞公郢、漢捉兵，即知揚州可得。

translations.literal: He Ruo Bi said to him: "When I heard you held troops at Ying and Han, I knew Yangzhou could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi told him, "When I learned you were holding the Ying and Han line, I knew Yangzhou would fall.

sentences.zh: 王師利涉，果如所量。」

translations.literal: When the royal army crossed the river with advantage, it was indeed as measured.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army crossed the river with ease, just as I had judged.

sentences.zh: 羅碶答曰：「若得與公周旋，勝負未可知也。」

translations.literal: Luohou replied: "If I could have matched wits with you, victory and defeat would not yet be knowable."
translations.idiomatic: Luohou replied, "Had I been able to meet you in battle, the outcome might still have been in doubt."

sentences.zh: 其年秋，拜上儀同三司，鼓吹送之於宅。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed Senior Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and imperial music escorted him to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed Senior Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and imperial musicians escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳裨將羊翔歸降，使為鄉導，位至開府，班在羅碶上。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen deputy general Yang Xiang had surrendered, was made a guide, reached the rank of Opening the Office, and stood in precedence above Luohou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen deputy general Yang Xiang had defected and served as a guide. He rose to the rank of Opening the Office and took precedence over Luohou.

sentences.zh: 韓禽於朝堂戲之曰：「不知機變，位在羊翔下。」

translations.literal: Han Qin in the court hall mocked him, saying: "Not knowing opportune change — rank below Yang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In court Han Qin mocked him, saying, "You did not know when to bend, and so you rank below Yang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 羅碶答曰：「昔在江南，久承令問，謂公天下節士。

translations.literal: Luohou replied: "Formerly in Jiangnan I long received your fine reputation and considered you a man of integrity under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou answered, "In Jiangnan I long admired your name and took you for a man of honor under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今日所言，殊匪人臣之論。」

translations.literal: What you say today is utterly unlike the discourse of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: What you say today is unworthy of a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 禽有愧色。

translations.literal: Qin had a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qin flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 曆幽、涇二州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of You and Jing — both with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of You and Jing, and in both posts earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年，征遼東，徵為水軍總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, when the campaign against Liaodong was launched, he was summoned as Commander-in-Chief of the Navy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, during the Liaodong campaign, he was summoned to serve as Commander-in-Chief of the Navy.

sentences.zh: 自東萊泛海趣平壤城，遭風，船多漂沒，入功而旋。

translations.literal: From Donglai he sailed across the sea toward Pyongyang; he encountered wind, many ships were washed away and sank, and he entered the campaign but turned back.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed from Donglai across the sea toward Pyongyang, but storms sank many of his ships, and he returned without achieving his objective.

sentences.zh: 十九年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，從楊素致討，羅碶先登，大破之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the Turkic Doutou Khan violated the frontier, he followed Yang Su to strike; Luohou ascended first and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when the Turkic khan Doutou raided the frontier, Luohou followed Yang Su to punish him, led the assault, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 進大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，入為東宮右虞候率，賜爵義寧郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou he entered service as Right Commandant-in-Chief of the Eastern Palace and was granted the title Duke of Yining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou he entered the Eastern Palace as Right Commandant-in-Chief and was ennobled as Duke of Yining commandery.

sentences.zh: 轉右衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Right Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授右武候大將軍，副楊素計平漢王諒，進授上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Command; he assisted Yang Su in planning to pacify Prince of Han Liang and was advanced to Senior Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Luohou was made Grand General of the Right Martial Command. Assisting Yang Su, he helped suppress Prince Liang of Han and was promoted to Senior Grand General.

sentences.zh: 及陳主卒，羅碶請一臨哭，帝許之。

translations.literal: When the former Chen ruler died, Luohou requested to come once to mourn; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the former Chen emperor died, Luohou asked leave to attend the mourning, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 衰絰送至墓，葬還，釋服而後入朝。

translations.literal: In mourning garments he escorted the bier to the tomb; after the burial he returned, doffed mourning garments, and only then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the tomb in full mourning, and only after the burial and the end of mourning did he return to court.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉尚之，世論稱其有禮。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and upheld him, and public opinion called him a man of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired him greatly, and public opinion praised his sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 時諒餘黨據絳、晉等三州未下，詔羅碶行晉、絳、呂三州諸軍事，進兵圍之。

translations.literal: At the time Liang's remaining partisans held Jiang, Jin, and other prefectures unstaken; an edict made Luohou conduct military affairs of Jin, Jiang, and Lü prefectures and advance troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liang's remaining followers still held Jiang, Jin, and other prefectures. An edict put Luohou in command of military affairs in Jin, Jiang, and Lü and ordered him to advance and besiege them.

sentences.zh: 中流矢，卒。

translations.literal: He was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow found him, and he fell dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 送柩還京，行數里，無故輿馬自止，策之不動，不飄風旋繞焉。

translations.literal: Escorting the bier back to the capital, after several li for no reason the carriage and horses stopped of themselves; whipping them, they would not move; windless whirlwinds circled around.
translations.idiomatic: As the coffin was being carried back to the capital, the carriage halted after a few li for no apparent reason. The drivers whipped the horses, but they would not move, while windless eddies spun around them.

sentences.zh: 絳州長史郭雅稽首祝曰：「公恨小寇未平邪？

translations.literal: Jiang prefecture chief administrator Guo Ya kowtowed and prayed, saying: "Does my lord regret that the small bandits are not yet pacified?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang prefecture chief administrator Guo Ya kowtowed and prayed, "My lord, do you grieve that the rebels are not yet destroyed?

sentences.zh: 尋既除殄，無為戀恨。」

translations.literal: Soon they will be eliminated and destroyed — do not cling to regret.
translations.idiomatic: They will soon be wiped out. Do not linger in resentment.

sentences.zh: 是時風靜馬行，見者莫不悲歎。

translations.literal: At that time the wind stilled and the horses moved; viewers none did not grieve and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: At once the wind fell still and the horses moved on. All who saw it were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，子仲隱夢羅碶曰：「我明日當戰。」

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month, his son Zhongyin dreamed that Luohou said: "Tomorrow I shall fight.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month his son Zhongyin dreamed that Luohou said, "Tomorrow I shall fight.

sentences.zh: 其靈坐所有弓箭刀劍無故自動，若人帶持之狀。

translations.literal: At his spirit seat all bows, arrows, swords, and blades for no reason moved of themselves, as if a person were wearing and holding them.
translations.idiomatic: At the spirit seat, his bows, arrows, swords, and blades moved of their own accord, as though a man were girding and wielding them.

sentences.zh: 絳州城陷，是其日也。

translations.literal: Jiang prefecture city fell — it was that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang prefecture fell that very day.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國、右翊衛大將軍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Pillar of the State and Grand General of the Right Wing Guard; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles Pillar of the State and Grand General of the Right Wing Guard, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子仲安，位上開府。

translations.literal: His son Zhong'an held the rank of Senior Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong'an rose to the rank of Senior Opening the Office.

sentences.zh: 周法尚，字德邁，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fashang, courtesy name Demai, was a man of Ancheng in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fashang, whose courtesy name was Demai, came from Ancheng in Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖靈起，梁廬、桂二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingqi was Governor of the two provinces Lu and Gui under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingqi had served as governor of Lu and Gui, the two Liang provinces.

sentences.zh: 父炅，定州刺史、平北將軍。

translations.literal: His father Jiong was Governor of Dingzhou and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiong held the posts of governor of Dingzhou and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 法尚少果勁，有風概，好讀兵書。

translations.literal: Fashang in youth was resolute and vigorous, had bearing and presence, and loved reading books of war.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fashang was bold and forceful, carried himself with authority, and loved to study military texts.

sentences.zh: 其父卒後，監定州事，督父本兵。

translations.literal: After his father died, he supervised affairs of Dingzhou and commanded his father's original troops.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he took charge of Dingzhou and led the troops his father had commanded.

sentences.zh: 數有戰功，為散騎常侍，領齊昌郡事，封山陰縣侯。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he had battle merit; he became Attendant Cavalier, oversaw affairs of Qichang commandery, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyin county.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated victories in battle, was made Attendant Cavalier and put in charge of Qichang commandery, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyin county.

sentences.zh: 既而其兄武昌縣公法僧代為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his elder brother Faseng, Duke of Wuchang county, replaced him as Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his elder brother Faseng, Duke of Wuchang county, succeeded him as governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 法尚與長沙王叔堅不相能，叔堅言其將反。

translations.literal: Fashang and Prince of Changsha Shujian did not get along; Shujian said that he would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang and Prince of Changsha Shujian were at odds, and Shujian accused him of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝執禁法僧，發兵欲取法尚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen arrested and imprisoned Faseng, and sent troops intending to seize Fashang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen had Faseng arrested and imprisoned, then raised an army to capture Fashang.

sentences.zh: 其下將吏皆勸之歸北，法尚未決。

translations.literal: All his subordinate officers urged him to defect north, but Fashang had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all urged him to defect to the north, yet Fashang could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 長史殷文則曰：「樂毅所以辭燕，良不獲已也。」

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Yin Wenzhe said: "The reason Yue Yi left Yan was truly that he had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Yin Wenzhe said, "When Yue Yi left Yan, it was only because he had no other choice.

sentences.zh: 法尚遂歸周，拜開府、順州刺史，封歸義縣公，賜良馬五匹、女妓六人、彩物五百段，加以金帶。

translations.literal: Fashang then defected to Zhou; he was appointed Grand Opening and Governor of Shunzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyi county, granted five fine horses, six female entertainers, and five hundred lengths of colored goods, and given a gold girdle besides.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang then went over to Northern Zhou. He was made Grand Opening and governor of Shunzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyi county, and rewarded with five fine horses, six female entertainers, five hundred lengths of colored silk, and a gold girdle.

sentences.zh: 陳將樊猛濟江討之，法尚遣部曲督朗韓朗詐為背己奔陳，偽告猛曰：「法尚部兵不願降北，若得軍來，必無鬥者。」

translations.literal: Chen general Fan Meng crossed the river to attack him; Fashang sent his retainer commander Han Lang of Lang to feign desertion to Chen and falsely tell Meng, "The troops under Fashang do not wish to surrender to the north; if an army comes, there will certainly be no one to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Fan Meng crossed the Yangzi to attack him. Fashang sent his retainer commander Han Lang of Lang to pretend to desert to Chen and falsely tell Meng, "Fashang's men do not want to surrender to the north. If your army comes, none of them will fight.

sentences.zh: 猛引師急進。

translations.literal: Meng led his army forward in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Meng hurried his army forward.

sentences.zh: 法尚設奇兵，大敗之，猛僅以身免。

translations.literal: Fashang set an ambush force and routed them utterly; Meng barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang laid an ambush and crushed the Chen force. Meng escaped only with his life.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，司馬消難作亂，陰遣上開府段珣攻圍之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Sima Xiaonan rose in rebellion; Wen secretly sent Senior Opening Duan Xun to attack and besiege Fashang.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen of Sui was still chief minister, Sima Xiaonan rebelled, and Wen secretly sent Senior Opening Duan Xun to attack and besiege Fashang.

sentences.zh: 外無救援，法尚棄城走。

translations.literal: With no relief from outside, Fashang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: No relief came from outside, and Fashang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 消難虜其母弟及家累三百人歸陳。

translations.literal: Xiaonan captured his mother, younger brother, and three hundred dependents and took them back to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan captured Fashang's mother, younger brother, and three hundred dependents and carried them off to Chen.

sentences.zh: 及文帝受禪，拜巴州刺史，破三鵶叛蠻，復從柱國王誼擊走陳寇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, Fashang was appointed Governor of Bazhou, defeated the rebellious Three Geese barbarians, and again followed Pillar of State Wang Yi in driving off Chen raiders.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen took the throne, Fashang was made governor of Bazhou. He crushed the rebellious Three Geese tribes and again followed Pillar of State Wang Yi in repelling Chen invaders.

sentences.zh: 遷衡州總管，改封譙郡公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Regional Commander of Hengzhou, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Hengzhou, and his title was changed to Duke of Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 後上幸洛陽，召之，賜金鈿酒鐘一雙、彩五百段、良馬十五匹、奴婢三百口，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor visited Luoyang, he summoned Fashang and granted him a pair of gold-inlaid wine vessels, five hundred lengths of colored goods, fifteen fine horses, three hundred slaves, and a full set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor visited Luoyang, Fashang was summoned and given a pair of gold-inlaid wine vessels, five hundred lengths of colored silk, fifteen fine horses, three hundred slaves, and a full band of trumpets and drums.

sentences.zh: 法尚固辭。

translations.literal: Fashang firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang firmly declined the honor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公有大功于國，特給鼓吹者，欲公卿知朕之寵公也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have great merit for the state. I grant martial music especially so that the ministers will know how I favor you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have rendered great service to the state. I am granting you martial music so that the court will know how highly I favor you.

sentences.zh: 轉黃州總管，使經略江南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Commander of Huangzhou and charged with managing strategy in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made regional commander of Huangzhou and charged with securing Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 及伐陳之役，以行軍總管隸秦孝王。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he served as Army Campaign Commander under Prince of Qin Xiaowang.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Chen he served as army campaign commander under Prince of Qin Xiaowang.

sentences.zh: 轉鄂州刺史，遷永州總管，安集嶺南，仍給黃州兵三千五百人為帳內。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Ezhou, then moved to Regional Commander of Yongzhou to pacify and gather Lingnan; he was still given three thousand five hundred Huangzhou troops as his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Ezhou, then made regional commander of Yongzhou to pacify Lingnan, with three thousand five hundred Huangzhou troops assigned as his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Before and after, his rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded lavishly, again and again.

sentences.zh: 轉柱州總管，仍嶺南道安撫大使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Commander of Zhuzhou and also made Pacification Commissioner of the Lingnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regional commander of Zhuzhou and also appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Lingnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 後數年入朝，以本官宿衛。

translations.literal: Several years later he came to court and, retaining his original office, performed palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he came to court and, while keeping his rank, took up palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，桂州人李光仕反，令法尚與上柱國王世積討之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Guangshi of Guizhou rebelled, and Fashang was ordered, together with Pillar of State Wang Shiji, to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Guangshi of Guizhou rebelled, and Fashang was ordered to join Pillar of State Wang Shiji in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 法尚發嶺南兵，世積徵嶺北軍。

translations.literal: Fashang mobilized Lingnan troops, and Shiji summoned Lingbei armies.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang raised troops from south of the ranges, while Shiji gathered armies from the north.

sentences.zh: 俱會尹州。

translations.literal: Both met at Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The two forces rendezvoused at Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 世積所部多遇瘴，不能進，頓於衡州。

translations.literal: Most of the troops under Shiji encountered miasma and could not advance; they halted at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Shiji's men fell sick with miasma and could not advance, so they halted at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 法尚獨討之，捕得其弟光略、光度，追斬光仕，平之。

translations.literal: Fashang alone pursued the campaign, captured Guangshi's younger brothers Guanglue and Guangdu, hunted down and killed Guangshi, and pacified the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang pursued the rebels alone, captured Guangshi's brothers Guanglue and Guangdu, hunted down and killed Guangshi, and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 仕壽中，遂州獠叛，復以行軍總管討平之。

translations.literal: While still in office during the Renshou era, the Liao of Suizhou rebelled, and again as Army Campaign Commander he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era, while he was still in office, the Liao of Suizhou rebelled, and again as army campaign commander he put them down.

sentences.zh: 巂州烏蠻反，詔法尚便道討擊破之。

translations.literal: The Black Liao of Xizhou rebelled, and an edict ordered Fashang to strike them by the direct route and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Black Liao of Xizhou rebelled, an edict ordered Fashang to take the direct route, attack them, and crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 軍還，檢校潞州事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was made acting inspector of Luzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was appointed acting inspector of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉雲州刺史，遷定襄太守，進金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Fashang was transferred to Governor of Yunzhou, moved to Governor of Dingxiang, and promoted to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Fashang was made governor of Yunzhou, then governor of Dingxiang, and promoted to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 時帝幸榆林，法尚朝於行宮。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor visited Yulin, and Fashang attended court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Yulin, Fashang came to audience at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 內史令元壽言於帝曰：「漢武出塞，旌旗千里。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Yuan Shou said to the emperor: "When Han Wudi went beyond the frontier, his banners stretched for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Yuan Shou said to the emperor, "When Emperor Wu of Han marched beyond the frontier, his banners stretched for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 今御營外，請分為二十四軍，日別遣一軍發，相雲三十里，旗幟相望，鉦鼓相聞，首尾連注，千里不絕。」

translations.literal: Outside the imperial encampment now, I ask that it be divided into twenty-four armies, with one army sent out each day, each thirty li apart, banners facing one another, gongs and drums within hearing, head and tail linked in succession without break for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the imperial camp, let the force be divided into twenty-four armies, with one army setting out each day, each thirty li behind the last, so that banners face one another, gongs and drums can be heard from camp to camp, and the line stretches unbroken for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 法尚曰：「兵亙千里，動間山谷，卒有不虞，四分五裂，腹心有事，首尾未知。

translations.literal: Fashang said: "An army stretched a thousand li, with movement spanning valleys — if suddenly something unforeseen occurs, it will split apart; if trouble strikes the center, head and tail will not know.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang said, "An army strung out for a thousand li, moving through valleys — if disaster strikes suddenly, the line will break apart. If trouble hits the center, the front and rear will not even know.

sentences.zh: 雖有故事，此取敗道也。」

translations.literal: Although there is precedent, this is the path to defeat."
translations.idiomatic: There may be precedent for it, but this is a recipe for disaster."

sentences.zh: 帝不懌曰：「卿以為如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "What do you think should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor said, "What do you propose instead?"

sentences.zh: 法尚曰：「請為方陣，四面外拒，六宮及百官家口並住其間。

translations.literal: Fashang said: "I ask that a square formation be made, resisting outward on all four sides, with the Six Palaces and the households of all officials lodged within it.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang said, "Form a square camp, facing outward on all four sides, with the imperial consorts and the families of the officials sheltered inside.

sentences.zh: 若有變，當頭分抗，車為壁壘，重設鉤陳，此與據城何異？

translations.literal: If there is trouble, resist separately at the front; use wagons as ramparts and set up layered Gouchen formations — how is this different from holding a city?
translations.idiomatic: If attack comes, each front can resist on its own. Wagons become ramparts, and layered defensive formations are set in place. How is that different from holding a walled city?

sentences.zh: 臣謂牢固萬全策也。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers this a firm and wholly secure plan."
translations.idiomatic: In my view, that would be the safest plan of all."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 因拜左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang was then appointed General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，黔安夷向思多反，殺將軍鹿願，圍太守蕭造。

translations.literal: The next year Xiang Siduo of the Qian'an Yi rebelled, killed General Lu Yuan, and besieged Governor Xiao Zao.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xiang Siduo of the Qian'an Yi rebelled, killed General Lu Yuan, and besieged Governor Xiao Zao.

sentences.zh: 法尚與將軍李景分路討之，法尚破思多於清江。

translations.literal: Fashang and General Li Jing suppressed them by separate routes; Fashang defeated Siduo at Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang and General Li Jing attacked by separate routes, and Fashang defeated Siduo at Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 及還，從討吐谷渾，別出松州道，逐捕亡散，至於青海。

translations.literal: On his return he followed the campaign against Tuyuhun, separately taking the Songzhou route, pursuing and capturing fugitives and stragglers as far as Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he joined the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Songzhou route separately to hunt down fugitives as far as Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 出為敦煌太守，遷會甯太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Dunhuang, then was transferred to Governor of Huining.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Dunhuang, then transferred to governor of Huining.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以舟師指朝鮮道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he commanded the naval force toward the Korea route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he led the fleet toward Korea.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感反，與宇文述、來護等破之。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan rebelled, and together with Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and the others he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he joined Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and the others in crushing the revolt.

sentences.zh: 以功進授右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted and granted the title Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時齊郡人王薄、孟讓等為盜，保長白山，法尚頻擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Bo and Meng Rang of Qi commandery became bandits, held Mount Changbai, and Fashang repeatedly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Bo, Meng Rang, and others of Qi commandery turned bandit, held Mount Changbai, and Fashang repeatedly routed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，復臨滄海，在軍遇疾卒。

translations.literal: The next year he again went to the Eastern Sea; in the army he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again went to the coast, but fell ill in camp and died.

sentences.zh: 贈武衛大將軍，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General of the Martial Guard; posthumous title Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand General of the Martial Guard, with the posthumous name Xi.

sentences.zh: 有子六人，紹范最知名。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Shaofan was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons, of whom Shaofan was the best known.

sentences.zh: 衛玄，字文升，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Xuan, courtesy name Wensheng, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan, whose courtesy name was Wensheng, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，魏司農卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Minister of Revenues under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue had been Minister of Revenues under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父舣，侍中、左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 玄少有器識，周武帝在籓，引為記室。

translations.literal: Xuan in youth had capacity and discernment; when Emperor Wu of Zhou was in his princely fief, he summoned him as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xuan showed talent and judgment. While Emperor Wu of Zhou was still a prince, he took Xuan on as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷給事上士，襲爵興勢公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Senior Clerk and inherited the title Duke of Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Senior Clerk and inherited the title Duke of Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜益州總管長史，賜以萬釘寶帶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally managed all affairs of state, Xuan was appointed Chief Clerk to the Regional Commander of Yizhou and granted a precious belt studded with ten thousand nails.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal charge of government, Xuan was made chief clerk to the regional commander of Yizhou and given a precious belt studded with ten thousand gold nails.

sentences.zh: 稍遷開府儀同三司、太府中大夫，攝內史事，仍領京兆尹，稱為強濟。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Opening with Equal Third Rank, Grand Master of the Treasury, acting director of the Secretariat affairs, and still Prefect of Jingzhao; he was called forceful and efficient.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Opening with Equal Third Rank and Grand Master of the Treasury, served as acting director of the Secretariat while still holding the post of prefect of Jingzhao, and was known for being forceful and effective.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，檢校熊州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chief minister, Xuan was made acting inspector of Xiongzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Xuan was appointed acting inspector of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷淮州總管，進封同軌郡公，坐事免。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, he was transferred to Regional Commander of Huaizhou, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Tonggui commandery, and then dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication he was made regional commander of Huaizhou and advanced to Duke of Tonggui commandery, but was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed governor of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會起長城之役，詔玄監督之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Great Wall project was launched, and an edict ordered Xuan to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the Great Wall began, an edict put Xuan in charge of supervising it.

sentences.zh: 後為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became vice director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，山獠作逆，以玄為資州刺史，以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, the mountain Liao rebelled, and Xuan was made Governor of Zizhou to pacify and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era, when the mountain Liao rebelled, Xuan was made governor of Zizhou to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 玄既到官，時獠攻圍大牢鎮，玄單騎造其營，謂群獠曰：「我是刺史，銜天子詔安養汝等，汝等勿驚」諸賊莫敢動。

translations.literal: Once Xuan had taken office, the Liao were at that time attacking and besieging Dalao fortress; Xuan went alone on horseback to their camp and said to the Liao as a group, "I am the governor, bearing the Son of Heaven's edict to settle and nourish you — do not be alarmed." None of the bandits dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuan had taken office, the Liao were besieging Dalao fortress. He rode alone into their camp and told the assembled tribesmen, "I am your governor. I come bearing the Son of Heaven's edict to settle and care for you. Do not be afraid." Not one of the rebels dared stir.

sentences.zh: 於是說以利害，渠帥感悅，解兵歸附者十餘萬口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he explained advantage and harm; the chieftains were moved and pleased, and more than one hundred thousand who laid down arms and submitted followed.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained what they stood to gain or lose. The chieftains were won over, and more than one hundred thousand laid down their arms and submitted.

sentences.zh: 文帝大悅，賜縑二千匹，除遂州總管，仍令劍南安撫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased, granted two thousand lengths of silk, appointed him Regional Commander of Suizhou, and still charged him with pacification in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased, granted him two thousand lengths of silk, made him regional commander of Suizhou, and kept him in charge of pacifying Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 九年，駕幸遼東，使玄與代王侑留守京師，拜為京兆內史，尚書如故，許以便宜從事，敕代王待以師傅禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the imperial carriage visited Liaodong, Xuan was left with Prince of Dai You to guard the capital; he was appointed Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, retained his ministerial rank as before, granted discretionary authority, and ordered that the Prince of Dai treat him with a mentor's courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the emperor went to Liaodong, Xuan was left in the capital with Prince of Dai You. He was made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao while keeping his ministerial rank, granted discretionary authority, and ordered that the Prince of Dai treat him with the respect due a mentor.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感圍東都，玄率步騎七萬援之。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, and Xuan led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, Xuan led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to its relief.

sentences.zh: 至華陰，掘楊素塚，焚其骸骨，夷其塋域，示士卒以必死。

translations.literal: At Huayin he dug up the tomb of Yang Su, burned his bones, leveled the cemetery grounds, and showed the soldiers that they must fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin he opened Yang Su's tomb, burned the bones, and razed the graveyard, showing his men that they must fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 既出潼關，議者恐崤函有伏兵，請於陝縣沿流東下，直趨河陽，以攻其背。

translations.literal: After passing Tong Pass, those in council feared an ambush at the Xiao and Han passes and asked that at Shan county they go downstream eastward and strike straight for Heyang to attack the enemy's rear.
translations.idiomatic: After passing Tong Pass, his advisers feared an ambush in the Xiao and Han passes and urged him to go downstream from Shan county toward Heyang and attack the rebels from behind.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「此計非豎子所及也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "This plan is not something a stripling would conceive.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "That is not the sort of plan a stripling would devise.

sentences.zh: 乃鼓行而進。

translations.literal: He then advanced with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he marched forward with drums beating.

sentences.zh: 既度函谷，卒如所量。

translations.literal: After crossing Hangu Pass, it turned out exactly as he had judged.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Hangu Pass, events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 乃遣武賁郎將張峻為疑軍於南道，玄以大兵直趨城北。

translations.literal: He then sent Colonel of the Martial Guard Zhang Jun as a decoy force on the southern route, while Xuan with the main army struck straight for the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Colonel of the Martial Guard Zhang Jun with a decoy force along the southern route, while he himself led the main army straight toward the north of the city.

sentences.zh: 玄感逆拒之，且戰且行，屯軍金穀。

translations.literal: Xuangan met him in resistance, fighting as he went, and encamped his army at Jingu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan met him in battle, fighting as he withdrew, and encamped at Jingu.

sentences.zh: 於軍中掃地而祭文帝曰：「若社稷靈長，宜令醜徒冰碎；

translations.literal: In the army he swept the ground and sacrificed to Emperor Wen, saying, "If the altars of state endure, let the vile rebels be shattered like ice;
translations.idiomatic: In camp he swept the ground and offered sacrifice to Emperor Wen, saying, "If the altars of state endure, let these vile rebels be shattered like ice;

sentences.zh: 如或大運去矣，幸使老臣先死。」

translations.literal: but if the Great Mandate has departed, may this old minister die first.
translations.idiomatic: but if the Great Mandate has already passed away, then let this old servant die first.

sentences.zh: 詞氣激揚，三軍莫不涕咽。

translations.literal: His words were impassioned and soaring; throughout the three armies none failed to weep with choked voices.
translations.idiomatic: His words rang with fierce devotion, and soldiers throughout the army wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 時眾寡不敵，民賊頻戰不利，死傷太半。

translations.literal: At that time they were outnumbered; the rebel forces repeatedly fought without success, and more than half were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: They were heavily outnumbered. Battle after battle went against them, and more than half the army was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 玄苦戰，賊稍卻，進屯北芒。

translations.literal: Xuan fought bitterly, the rebels gradually fell back, and he advanced and encamped at Beimang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fought on grimly until the rebels began to give ground, then advanced and encamped at Beimang.

sentences.zh: 會宇文述、來護等援兵至，玄感西遁。

translations.literal: It happened that relief troops under Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and the others arrived, and Xuangan fled west.
translations.idiomatic: When relief troops under Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu, and the others arrived, Xuangan fled west.

sentences.zh: 玄遣通議大夫斛斯萬善、監門直閣龐玉前鋒追之，及於閿鄉，與宇文述等合擊破之。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Chief Gentleman of Discussion Husi Wanshan and Direct Attendant of the Gate Guard Pang Yu as vanguard in pursuit; they caught up at Wen village and, together with Yuwen Shu and the others, joined in attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Chief Gentleman of Discussion Husi Wanshan and Direct Attendant of the Gate Guard Pang Yu in pursuit at the vanguard. They caught Xuangan at Wen village and, joining with Yuwen Shu and the others, destroyed his force.

sentences.zh: 車駕至高陽，征詣行在所。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Gaoyang, Xuan was summoned to the traveling headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Gaoyang, Xuan was summoned to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「社稷臣也。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him, saying, "A pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, saying, "You are a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 使朕無西顧之憂。」

translations.literal: You have spared Us worry over the west.
translations.idiomatic: You have spared me all worry for the west.

sentences.zh: 進右光祿大夫，賜以良田、甲第，資物钜萬，還鎮京師，帝謂曰：「關右之任，一委於公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted fine fields and a noble mansion, and goods worth tens of thousands; returning to guard the capital, the emperor said to him, "The charge over Guan west I entrust entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given fine fields, a noble mansion, and goods worth a fortune. When he returned to guard the capital, the emperor told him, "The defense of the western passes I entrust entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 公安，社稷乃安；

translations.literal: If you are secure, the altars of state will be secure;
translations.idiomatic: If you are secure, the state is secure;

sentences.zh: 公危，社稷亦危。

translations.literal: if you are endangered, the altars of state are also endangered.
translations.idiomatic: if you are in peril, the state is in peril.

sentences.zh: 出入須有兵衛，坐臥恆宜自牢也。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in you must have armed guards; sitting and lying down you should always keep yourself secure.
translations.idiomatic: You must have armed guards whenever you go out or come in, and even in rest you must keep yourself well protected.

sentences.zh: 今特給千兵，以充侍從。」

translations.literal: Now I specially grant a thousand troops to serve as your attendants.
translations.idiomatic: I am therefore giving you a thousand troops as your personal guard.

sentences.zh: 與樊子蓋俱賜以玉麟符，以代銅獸。

translations.literal: Together with Fan Zigai he was granted jade unicorn tallies in place of the bronze beast ones.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fan Zigai were both granted jade unicorn tallies to replace the old bronze beast seals.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔玄撫關中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered Xuan to pacify and govern Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, an edict appointed Xuan to pacify and govern Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂起，百姓饑饉，玄竟不能救恤。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels swarmed like bees, the common people suffered famine, and in the end Xuan could not succor or relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and rebels were rising everywhere, the people were starving, and Xuan proved unable to help them.

sentences.zh: 而官方壞亂，貨賄公行。

translations.literal: Moreover official administration was ruined and disordered, and bribes circulated openly.
translations.idiomatic: Official administration collapsed, and bribery was practiced openly.

sentences.zh: 自以年老，上表乞骸骨，帝遣內史舍人封德彝馳喻之曰：「京師國本，宗廟園陵所在，籍公臥以鎮之。」

translations.literal: Thinking himself old, he submitted a memorial requesting to retire and return his bones; the emperor sent Palace Secretary Cadet Feng Deyi posthaste to persuade him, saying, "The capital is the foundation of the state, where the ancestral temples and imperial tombs stand — We rely on you, even in repose, to hold it firm.
translations.idiomatic: Concluding that he was too old, he submitted a memorial asking to retire. The emperor sent Palace Secretary Cadet Feng Deyi posthaste to persuade him, saying, "The capital is the foundation of the state, where the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie — I depend on you, even in repose, to hold it firm.

sentences.zh: 玄乃止。

translations.literal: Xuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then withdrew his request.

sentences.zh: 義師入關，自知不能守，尤懼稱疾，不知政事。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the pass, knowing he could not hold out, he was especially afraid and pleaded illness, paying no heed to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army entered the pass, knowing he could not hold the city, he took refuge in illness and ignored all affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 城陷，歸於家。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he went home.

sentences.zh: 義寧中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yining era, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yining period.

sentences.zh: 子孝則，位通事舍人、兵部承務郎。

translations.literal: His son Xiaze held the posts of Master of Accounts Attendant and Clerk of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaze served as Master of Accounts Attendant and Clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 劉權，字世略，彭城豐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Quan, courtesy name Shilue, was a native of Feng in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan, courtesy name Shilue, was from Feng in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖軌，齊羅州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Governor of Luo Province in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui had been Governor of Luo Province under Qi.

sentences.zh: 權少有俠氣，重然諾，藏亡匿死，吏不敢過門，。

translations.literal: In youth Quan had a chivalrous spirit, prized keeping his word, sheltered fugitives and hid the dead; officials did not dare pass his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Quan had a chivalrous spirit and prized his word. He sheltered fugitives and concealed the dead, and officials did not dare approach his gate.

sentences.zh: 後更折節好學，動循法度。

translations.literal: Later he changed his ways, bent his conduct, loved learning, and in action followed law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Later he reformed his conduct, took up learning, and in all his actions followed the law.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位行台郎中。

translations.literal: He served Qi and held the post of Staff Bureau Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Qi as a Staff Bureau Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，周武帝以為假淮州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made him Acting Governor of Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made him Acting Governor of Huai Province.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，以車騎將軍領鄉兵。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, as General of Chariots and Cavalry he led local militia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign, he served as General of Chariots and Cavalry commanding local militia.

sentences.zh: 後從晉王廣平陳，進授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince of Jin Guang in pacifying Chen and was promoted to Grand Master of Resplendent Happiness with the privileges of a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Prince Guang of Jin in the campaign against Chen and was promoted to Grand Master of Resplendent Happiness with the privileges of a separate office.

sentences.zh: 宋國公賀若弼甚禮之。

translations.literal: Duke of Song He Ruobi treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Song He Ruobi treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜蘇州刺史，賜爵宋城縣公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor of Su Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Songcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor of Su Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Songcheng County.

sentences.zh: 時江南初平，權撫以恩信，甚得人和。

translations.literal: At that time the south of the Yangzi had just been pacified; Quan soothed the people with kindness and good faith and won great harmony among them.
translations.idiomatic: The south of the Yangzi had just been pacified, and Quan won the people over with kindness and trust, achieving remarkable harmony.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜衛尉卿，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Quan was appointed Minister of the Guard and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he was appointed Minister of the Guard and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從征吐谷渾，權出伊吾道，逐賊至青海，乘勝至伏俟城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he followed the campaign against Tuyuhun; Quan took the Yiwu route, pursued the enemy to Qinghai, and pressing his advantage reached Fuyu City.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye he joined the campaign against Tuyuhun. Quan marched by the Yiwu route, pursued the enemy to Qinghai, and riding the momentum reached Fuyu City.

sentences.zh: 帝復令權過曼頭、赤水，置河源郡、積石鎮，大開屯田，留鎮西境。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Quan to pass Mantou and Chishui, establish Heyuan Commandery and Jishi Garrison, greatly open military colonies, and remain to garrison the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Quan to pass Mantou and Chishui, establish Heyuan Commandery and Jishi Garrison, expand military farming, and remain to guard the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 在邊五年，諸羌懷附，貢賦歲入，吐谷渾餘燼遠遁，道路無壅。

translations.literal: On the frontier for five years, the various Qiang came with hearts attached, tribute and levies entered every year, the embers of Tuyuhun fled far away, and the roads were unobstructed.
translations.idiomatic: After five years on the frontier, the Qiang tribes had submitted willingly, annual tribute flowed in, the remnants of Tuyuhun had fled far away, and the roads were clear.

sentences.zh: 徵拜司農卿，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Minister of Public Revenue, he was further given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Gold Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Minister of Public Revenue, with the additional rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Gold Seal.

sentences.zh: 尋為南海太守。

translations.literal: Soon after he became Governor of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Governor of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 行至鄱陽，會群盜起，不得進，詔權召募討之。

translations.literal: When he reached Poyang, bandits rose in groups, he could not advance, and an edict ordered Quan to recruit troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Poyang he found bandits rising everywhere and could not continue. An edict ordered him to raise troops and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 權率兵遇賊，不戰，先乘單舸詣賊營，說以利害。

translations.literal: Quan led troops and met the bandits; without fighting, he first took a lone boat to their camp and reasoned with them about gain and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Quan led his troops to the bandits but did not fight. Instead he took a single boat to their camp and argued the costs and benefits of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 群賊感悅，一時降附。

translations.literal: The bandits were moved and pleased and surrendered all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were won over and surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and praised him.

sentences.zh: 及至南海，甚有異政。

translations.literal: When he reached Nanhai he achieved many remarkable feats of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Nanhai he governed with notable distinction.

sentences.zh: 數歲，遇盜賊群起，群豪多願推權為首，權竟固守以拒之。

translations.literal: After several years bandits rose in groups; many local magnates wished to make Quan their leader, but Quan steadfastly held firm and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: After several years bandits rose everywhere, and many local leaders wanted to make Quan their chief, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 子世徹又密遣齎人書詣權，稱四方擾亂，諷令舉兵。

translations.literal: His son Shiche also secretly sent a man bearing a letter to Quan, declaring disturbance throughout the four quarters and hinting that he should raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiche also secretly sent a messenger with a letter urging him to take up arms, citing turmoil throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 權召集佐僚，對斬其使，竟無異圖，守之以死。

translations.literal: Quan summoned his aides and staff, beheaded the messenger before them, never harbored a rebellious plan, and defended to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Quan assembled his aides, executed the messenger before them, never wavered in loyalty, and defended the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 世徹倜儻不羈，頗為時人所許。

translations.literal: Shiche was unrestrained and free-spirited, and was much admired by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shiche was bold and unconventional, and many contemporaries admired him.

sentences.zh: 大業末，群雄並起，世徹所至處輒見忌，多拘禁之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, rival heroes rose together; wherever Shiche went he was envied and mostly detained.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign, as rival powers rose everywhere, Shiche was resented wherever he went and was often imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 後竟為兗州賊帥徐圓朗所殺。

translations.literal: In the end he was killed by Xu Yuanlang, bandit chief of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually killed by Xu Yuanlang, a rebel leader in Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 權從叔烈，字子將，美容儀，有器局，位鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: Quan's paternal cousin Lie, courtesy name Zijiang, had fine looks and bearing, possessed capacity and breadth of vision, and held the post of Colonel of the Striking Falcon.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's paternal cousin Lie, courtesy name Zijiang, was handsome and commanding in presence, and served as Colonel of the Striking Falcon.

sentences.zh: 有子德威，知名於世。

translations.literal: He had a son Dewei, known throughout the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Dewei, who became widely known.

sentences.zh: 李景，字道興，天水休官人也。

translations.literal: Li Jing, courtesy name Daoxing, was a native of Xiuguan in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, courtesy name Daoxing, was from Xiuguan in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父超，周應、戎二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chao was Governor of both Ying and Rong Provinces under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao had served as Governor of Ying and Rong Provinces under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 景容貌奇偉，膂力過人，美須髯，驍勇善射。

translations.literal: Jing's appearance was strangely grand, his physical strength surpassed others, his beard and whiskers were fine, and he was fierce and brave and skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was strikingly imposing in appearance, exceptionally strong, with a fine beard, and was valiant and skilled with the bow.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，頗有功，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi he achieved considerable merit and was granted the rank of Grand Master of the Third Order with the same privileges as a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Qi he distinguished himself and was granted the rank of Grand Master of the Third Order with the privileges of a separate office.

sentences.zh: 後以平尉遲迥，進位開府，賜爵平寇縣公。

translations.literal: Later for pacifying Yuwen Yong he was promoted to Grand Master with separate office and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingkou County.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in suppressing Yuwen Yong he was promoted to Grand Master with separate office and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingkou County.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇九年，以行軍總管從世積伐陳，以功進上開府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Sui Kaihuang, as Campaign Commander he followed Shi Ji in attacking Chen and, for his merit, was promoted to Senior Grand Master with separate office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, as Campaign Commander he followed Shi Ji against Chen and, for his achievements, was promoted to Senior Grand Master with separate office.

sentences.zh: 及高智慧等反，復以行軍總管從楊素擊之，還授鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, again as Campaign Commander he followed Yang Su in attacking them, and on return was appointed Governor of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, he again served as Campaign Commander under Yang Su, and afterward was appointed Governor of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遼東之役，為馬軍總管。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, during the Liaodong campaign, he served as Cavalry Commander.

sentences.zh: 及還，配事漢王。

translations.literal: On returning he was assigned to serve Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was assigned to serve the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 文帝奇其壯武，使袒而觀之，曰：「卿相表當位極人臣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen admired his stalwart martial bearing, had him bare his torso to look at him, and said, "By the physiognomy of minister and chancellor you ought to reach the highest rank among men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was struck by his imposing strength, had him bare his torso for inspection, and said, "The marks of a minister upon you point to the highest rank among men.

sentences.zh: 尋從史萬歲擊突厥於大斤山，別路邀賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed Shi Wansui in attacking the Turks at Mount Dajin, took a separate route to intercept the enemy, and defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Shi Wansui against the Turks at Mount Dajin, took a separate route to intercept the enemy, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 後與上明公楊紀送義城公主于突厥，至恆安，遇突厥來寇。

translations.literal: Later, together with Duke of Shangming Yang Ji, he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Turks; reaching Heng'an, they met a Turk raiding force.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Duke of Shangming Yang Ji escorted Princess Yicheng to the Turks. At Heng'an they encountered a Turk attack.

sentences.zh: 時代州總管韓洪為虜所敗，景率所領數百人力戰三日，殺虜甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time Dai Province Commander Han Hong had been defeated by the barbarians; Jing led several hundred men under his command and fought bitterly for three days, killing very many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai Province Commander Han Hong had already been routed by the enemy when Jing led several hundred men in fierce combat for three days and killed a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 改授韓州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Governor of Han Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Governor of Han Province.

sentences.zh: 以事王故，不之官。

translations.literal: Because he was serving the prince, he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was serving the prince, he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，檢校代州總管。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was acting Commander of Dai Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign he served as acting Commander of Dai Province.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒作亂，景發兵拒之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Jing raised troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, Jing mobilized troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 諒頻遣劉嵩、喬鐘葵等攻之，景率士卒殊死戰，屢挫賊鋒。

translations.literal: Liang repeatedly sent Liu Song, Qiao Zhongkui, and others to attack him; Jing led his soldiers in fight-to-the-death combat and repeatedly blunted the rebel spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Liang repeatedly sent Liu Song, Qiao Zhongkui, and others against him. Jing led his men in desperate fighting and repeatedly turned back the rebel attacks.

sentences.zh: 司馬馮孝慈、司法參軍呂玉並驍勇善戰，儀同三司侯莫陳乂多謀畫，工拒守之術。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Feng Xiaoci and Legal Advisor Lü Yu were both fierce and brave and skilled in battle; Grand Master of the Third Order with separate office Houmochen Yi was rich in stratagems and adept at the art of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Feng Xiaoci and Legal Advisor Lü Yu were both ferocious fighters, while Grand Master Houmochen Yi was a skilled strategist expert in defensive warfare.

sentences.zh: 景推誠此三人，無所關預，唯在閤持重，時出撫循而已。

translations.literal: Jing placed his trust wholly in these three men and intervened in nothing; he only held weight in the office and from time to time went out to soothe and comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jing trusted these three men completely and did not interfere. He held overall command from headquarters and occasionally went out to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 及朔州總管楊義臣援兵至，合擊大破之。

translations.literal: When relief troops under Shuozhou Commander Yang Yichen arrived, they joined in attack and routed the rebels utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When relief troops under Shuozhou Commander Yang Yichen arrived, they joined forces and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 先是，府內井中甃上生花如蓮，並有龍見，時變為鐵馬甲士。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the brickwork of a well within the headquarters lotus-like flowers had sprung up, dragons were also seen, and at times they changed into armored men on iron horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, lotus-like flowers had appeared on the brickwork of a well in headquarters, dragons were seen, and at times they transformed into armored warriors on iron horses.

sentences.zh: 又有神人長數丈見城下，跡長四尺五寸。

translations.literal: There was also a divine man several zhang tall seen below the city wall, with footprints four chi and five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: A supernatural figure several zhang tall was also seen below the city, leaving footprints four chi and five cun long.

sentences.zh: 景問巫者，巫者曰：「此不祥之物，來食血耳。」

translations.literal: Jing questioned a shaman; the shaman said, "These are inauspicious things that come to feed on blood.
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked a shaman, who said, "These are ill omens — creatures that come to feed on blood.

sentences.zh: 景大怒，推出之。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly angered and had him driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing flew into a rage and had him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 旬日而兵至，死者數萬。

translations.literal: Within ten days troops arrived, and the dead numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the army arrived, and tens of thousands fell dead.

sentences.zh: 景尋被徵，進柱國，拜右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Jing was soon summoned, promoted to Pillar of the State, and appointed General of the Right Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was soon recalled, promoted to Pillar of the State, and appointed General of the Right Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 賜女樂一部，加以珍物。

translations.literal: He was granted a troupe of female musicians and also given precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a troupe of female musicians and many precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 景智略非所長，而忠直為時所許，帝甚信之。

translations.literal: Strategy and planning were not Jing's strong points, but his loyalty and directness were praised by the age, and the emperor trusted him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Strategy was not Jing's strength, but his loyalty and forthrightness won wide esteem, and the emperor trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 又擊破叛蠻向思多。

translations.literal: He also defeated the rebellious Man chieftain Xiang Siduo.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the rebel Man chieftain Xiang Siduo.

sentences.zh: 明年，擊吐谷渾于青海，破之，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked Tuyuhun at Qinghai, defeated them, and was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Tuyuhun at Qinghai, defeated them, and was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西巡，至天水，景獻食於帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage toured west to Tianshui, and Jing presented food to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor toured west to Tianshui, where Jing presented a feast.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公，主人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Sir, you are the host.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You, sir, are the host here.

sentences.zh: 賜坐齊王暕上。

translations.literal: He was granted a seat above Prince of Qi Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a seat of honor above Prince Kan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 至隴川宮，帝將大獵，景與左武衛大將軍郭衍俱有難色，為人奏。

translations.literal: Reaching Longchuan Palace, when the emperor was about to hold a great hunt, Jing and General of the Left Military Guard Guo Yan both showed troubled expressions and were reported by someone.
translations.idiomatic: At Longchuan Palace, when the emperor was preparing a grand hunt, Jing and General of the Left Military Guard Guo Yan both looked uneasy, and someone reported them.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，令Ξ之，竟以坐免。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered them beaten with rods; in the end Jing was dismissed on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered them flogged; Jing was eventually dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復位，與宇文述等參掌選舉。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to office and, together with Yuwen Shu and others, shared in supervising appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was restored to office and, with Yuwen Shu and others, shared control over official appointments.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻高麗武列城，破之，賜爵苑丘侯。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked Wulie City in Goguryeo, captured it, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Wulie City in Goguryeo, took it, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanqiu.

sentences.zh: 八年，出渾彌道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he set out by the Hunmi route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched out by the Hunmi route.

sentences.zh: 九年，復出遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again marched out to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again marched into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 及旋，使景殿，高麗追兵大至，景擊走之。

translations.literal: On the return march the emperor put Jing in the rear guard; Goguryeo pursuit troops arrived in force and Jing drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the emperor placed Jing in the rear guard. When Goguryeo pursuit forces arrived in strength, Jing drove them back.

sentences.zh: 進爵滑國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Huaguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Huaguo.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反，朝臣子弟多預焉，景獨無關涉。

translations.literal: In Yang Xuangan's rebellion many sons of court ministers took part, but Jing alone had no involvement.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, many sons of court officials joined him, but Jing alone had no part in it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公誠直天然，我梁棟也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Sir, your sincerity and directness are natural to you — you are Our beam and pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your honesty is inborn — you are my pillar and beam.

sentences.zh: 賜以美女。

translations.literal: He was granted beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: He was given beautiful women as a reward.

sentences.zh: 帝每呼李大將軍而不名，見重如此。

translations.literal: The emperor always called him Great General Li without using his given name — such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always addressed him as Great General Li rather than by name — so highly was he valued.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝令景營遼東戰具于北平，賜御馬一匹，名師子垆吉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor ordered Jing to prepare Liaodong war materiel at Beiping and granted him one imperial horse named Shizi Luji.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor ordered Jing to prepare war supplies for Liaodong at Beiping and gave him an imperial horse named Shizi Luji.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊蜂起，景遂召募，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels swarmed like bees; Jing then recruited troops to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits rising everywhere, Jing raised troops as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將羅藝與景有隙，誣景將反。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Martial Guard Luo Yi had a grudge against Jing and slandered him, saying he was about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Martial Guard Luo Yi bore a grudge against Jing and falsely accused him of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝遣其子慰諭曰：「縱人言公窺天闕，據京都，吾無疑也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent his son to comfort and instruct him, saying, "Even if people say you are eyeing the imperial gate and holding the capital, I have no doubt of you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his son to reassure him, saying, "Even if people claim you are scheming against the throne and seizing the capital, I do not doubt you.

sentences.zh: 後為高開道所圍，獨守孤城，士卒患腳腫死者十六七，景撫循之，一無離叛。

translations.literal: Later he was besieged by Gao Kaidao, alone held an isolated city; of the soldiers sixteen or seventeen out of ten suffered swollen feet and died, yet Jing soothed and comforted them and not one deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, besieged by Gao Kaidao in an isolated city, sixteen or seventeen soldiers out of every ten died of swollen feet, yet Jing cared for them so devotedly that not one deserted.

sentences.zh: 遼東軍資多在其所，粟帛山積，景無所私焉。

translations.literal: Much of the Liaodong army's supplies were stored where he was; grain and cloth piled like mountains, yet Jing took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Liaodong campaign supplies were stored in his territory — grain and cloth piled like mountains — yet Jing took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩于江都，遼西太守鄧皓救之，遂歸柳城。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Liaoxi Governor Deng Hao rescued him, and he then returned to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor died at Jiangdu, Liaoxi Governor Deng Hao came to his relief, and he returned to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 將還幽州，遇賊見害。

translations.literal: As he was about to return to You Province he met bandits and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back to You Province he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 契丹、靺鞨素感其恩，聞之莫不流涕；

translations.literal: The Khitan and Mohe had long felt his kindness; on hearing of it none failed to shed tears;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and Mohe, who had long felt his kindness, wept on hearing the news;

sentences.zh: 幽、燕人士，於今傷惜之。

translations.literal: men of You and Yan to this day mourn and lament him.
translations.idiomatic: and the people of You and Yan still mourn him to this day.

sentences.zh: 子世謨。

translations.literal: His son Shimuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shimuo.

sentences.zh: 薛世雄，字世英，本河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Shixiong, courtesy name Shiying, was originally a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shixiong, courtesy name Shiying, was originally from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其先寓居敦煌。

translations.literal: His ancestors had long resided in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 父回，字道弘，仕周，位涇州刺史。
