translations.literal: His father Hui, style name Daohong, served Zhou and held the post of governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, styled Daohong, had served Zhou as governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，封舞陰郡公，領漕渠監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyin commandery and led the canal transport office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyin and placed in charge of the canal transport office.

sentences.zh: 世雄兒童時與群輩戲，輒畫地為城郭，令諸兒為攻守勢，不從令者輒撻之，諸兒畏憚，莫不齊整。

translations.literal: When Shixiong was a child playing with his companions, he would draw walls and cities on the ground, set the boys to attack and defend, and whip those who disobeyed; the boys feared him and none failed to keep ranks.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Shixiong would play war games with his friends, sketching walls and cities in the dirt and drilling them in attack and defense; he flogged anyone who disobeyed, and they all fell into line in fear of him.

sentences.zh: 其父見而奇之，謂人曰：「此兒當興吾家。」

translations.literal: His father saw this and marveled, saying to others, "This boy will raise our house.
translations.idiomatic: His father saw it and was astonished. "This boy," he said, "will bring glory to our family.

sentences.zh: 年十七，從周武帝平齊，以功拜帥都督。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and for merit was appointed commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in the conquest of Qi and was made a commander-in-chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，累遷右親衛車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang under Sui he was repeatedly promoted to cavalry general of the right intimate guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he rose steadily to cavalry general of the right intimate guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，為右監門郎將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he became commandant of the right gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne he was made commandant of the right gate guard.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，進位通議大夫。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Tuyuhun he was advanced to general consultant.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he was promoted to general consultant.

sentences.zh: 世雄性廉慎，行軍破敵之處，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Shixiong's nature was incorrupt and cautious; wherever his army marched and defeated the enemy, not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong was scrupulously honest; on campaign he allowed no looting whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 帝由是嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor on this account praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂群臣曰：「欲舉好人，諸君識否？」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to his ministers, "I wish to promote a worthy man—do you know whom I mean?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked his ministers, "I mean to promote a worthy man—do any of you know whom I have in mind?

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「不測聖心。」

translations.literal: They all said, "We cannot fathom Your Majesty's intent."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We cannot guess Your Majesty's mind."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我欲舉薛世雄。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I wish to promote Xue Shixiong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I mean to promote Xue Shixiong."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆稱善。

translations.literal: The ministers all declared it good.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all applauded the choice.

sentences.zh: 於是超拜右翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted by special appointment to general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon promoted out of turn to general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為玉門道行軍大將軍，與突厥啟人可汗邊兵擊伊吾。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was made grand general on campaign of the Yumen route, and with the frontier troops of the Turkish Qiren qaghan attacked Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand campaign general on the Yumen route and, with Turkish Qiren frontier troops, attacked Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 師次玉門，啟人背約，兵不至。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yumen, Qiren broke the treaty and his troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: At Yumen the Qiren broke their agreement and never sent the promised troops.

sentences.zh: 世雄孤軍度磧。

translations.literal: Shixiong with a lone army crossed the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong crossed the desert with his army alone.

sentences.zh: 伊吾懼，請降。

translations.literal: Yiwu was afraid and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 世雄遂于漢舊伊吾城東築城，號新伊吾，留銀青光祿大夫王威鎮之而還。

translations.literal: Shixiong then east of the old Han city of Yiwu built a city called New Yiwu, left Silver Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Wei to garrison it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He built a new city east of the old Han Yiwu, called it New Yiwu, left Wang Wei to garrison it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進位正議大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to rectifying consultant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to rectifying consultant.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，為沃沮道軍將，與宇文述同敗績於平壤。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was army commander of the Woju route and with Yuwen Shu suffered defeat together at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he commanded the Woju route army and, with Yuwen Shu, was defeated at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 還次白石山，為賊所圍百餘重，四面矢下如雨。

translations.literal: On the return he halted at Baishi Mountain and was surrounded by bandits in more than a hundred rings; arrows fell from all four sides like rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he was encircled at Baishi Mountain by rebels in layer upon layer of rings, arrows falling like rain from every side.

sentences.zh: 世雄以羸師為方陣，選勁騎二百縱擊，破之而還。

translations.literal: Shixiong with his weakened army formed a square formation, selected two hundred strong horsemen for a charge, broke them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He formed his weakened troops in a square, led two hundred picked horsemen in a charge, broke the encirclement, and got through.

sentences.zh: 所亡失多，竟坐免。

translations.literal: What was lost was great, and in the end he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His losses were heavy and he was eventually dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征遼東，拜右候衛將軍。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned in Liaodong and appointed him general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on another Liaodong campaign, he was made general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 兵指蹋頓道。

translations.literal: His troops took the Tadun route.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Tadun route.

sentences.zh: 軍至烏骨城，會楊玄感反，班師。

translations.literal: When the army reached Wugu city, Yang Xuangan rebelled and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When his army reached Wugu, Yang Xuangan rebelled and the force turned back.

sentences.zh: 帝至柳城，以世雄為東北道大使，行燕郡太守，鎮懷遠。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Liucheng, he made Shixiong envoy of the northeast route, acting governor of Yan commandery, garrisoning Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Liucheng the emperor made him northeast-route envoy and acting governor of Yan, with his base at Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 十年，復從帝至遼東，遷左禦衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again followed the emperor to Liaodong and was transferred to grand general of the left guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he again accompanied the emperor to Liaodong and was promoted to grand general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 仍領涿郡留守。

translations.literal: He still held the post of garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He continued as garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密逼東都，詔世雄率幽、薊精兵將擊之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi pressed the eastern capital; an edict ordered Shixiong to lead elite troops of You and Ji to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Mi threatened Luoyang; Shixiong was ordered to lead picked troops from You and Ji against him.

sentences.zh: 次河間，營于城南，竇建德率精銳數百，夜來襲之。

translations.literal: He halted at Hejian and encamped south of the city; Dou Jiande led several hundred picked men in a night attack.
translations.idiomatic: He camped south of Hejian when Dou Jiande struck at night with several hundred elite troops.

sentences.zh: 大敗。

translations.literal: He suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He was routed.

sentences.zh: 世雄與左右數十騎遁入河間城，慚恚發病。

translations.literal: Shixiong with several dozen horsemen of his staff fled into Hejian city; ashamed and enraged, he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong escaped into Hejian with a few dozen followers, then fell ill from shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 歸涿郡，卒。

translations.literal: He returned to Zhuo commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Zhuo and died there.

sentences.zh: 子萬述、萬淑、萬鈞、萬徹、萬備，並以驍武知名。

translations.literal: His sons Wanshu, Wanshu, Wanjun, Wanche, and Wanbei were all known for fierce martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Wanshu, Wanshu, Wanjun, Wanche, and Wanbei were all famed for their fighting skill.

sentences.zh: 論曰：段文振有周之日，早以武毅見知，隋氏之初，又以幹力受委，任兼文武，稱為諒直。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the days of Zhou, Duan Wenzhen was early known for martial resolution; at the beginning of Sui he was again entrusted for practical ability, his duties combining civil and military, and he was called upright and straightforward.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Under Zhou, Duan Wenzhen was early recognized for martial grit; at the founding of Sui he was entrusted again for his capacity, served in both civil and military roles, and was known as bluntly honest.

sentences.zh: 其高位厚秩，非虛致也。

translations.literal: His high rank and rich stipend were not attained in vain.
translations.idiomatic: His high rank and rich rewards were honestly earned.

sentences.zh: 來護幼懷倜儻，猛概抑揚，晚致勤王，驅馳畢力。

translations.literal: Lai Hu in youth harbored bold unconventionality, his fierce spirit rising and falling; in later years he came to serve the throne in crisis and drove himself to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Hu'er was daring from youth, his martial spirit always in motion; in his last years he raced to the dynasty's rescue and gave all his strength.

sentences.zh: 樓船制勝，掃勍敵如拾遺；

translations.literal: With tower ships he won victory, sweeping fierce foes as though picking up what was dropped;
translations.idiomatic: Victory by tower ship swept mighty enemies aside as if gathering lost objects;

sentences.zh: 閿鄉討亂，翦凶魁如摧朽。

translations.literal: at Wenxiang he suppressed rebellion, cutting down the chief villain as one breaks rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: at Wenxiang he crushed rebellion and cut down its leaders like rotted timber.

sentences.zh: 位班上將，顯居大國，道消遘難，忠至不渝，惜矣！

translations.literal: His rank reached grand general and he stood eminent in a great state; when the Way declined and disaster struck, his loyalty to the end did not waver—alas!
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the highest military rank and stood among the great of the realm; when the dynasty fell into ruin he never wavered in loyalty—a tragedy!

sentences.zh: 子蓋雅有幹局，質性方嚴，見義而勇，臨機能斷，保全邦邑，勤亦懋哉！

translations.literal: Zigai by nature had administrative capacity, his character stern and upright; seeing righteousness he was brave, facing opportunity he could decide, preserving districts and towns—his diligence was indeed admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Zigai had true administrative talent, a stern and upright nature, courage when justice demanded it, and decisiveness in crisis; he preserved cities and commanderies—his service was genuinely admirable!

sentences.zh: 羅碶忠亮之性，所在稱重，送往之節，義感人臣，死而有知，乃結草之義。

translations.literal: Luohou's nature was loyal and bright, and wherever he went he was esteemed; the propriety of his farewell moved the hearts of ministers—if the dead have awareness, this was the righteousness of tying grass.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou's loyalty and integrity won respect wherever he served; the propriety of his funeral rites moved all who witnessed them—if the dead can know, he fulfilled the old duty of repaying a debt in the grass.

sentences.zh: 法尚征伐四夷，亦足嘉焉。

translations.literal: Fashang's campaigns against the four barbarians are also worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang's campaigns against the frontier peoples are likewise praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 文升東都解圍，頗亦宣力，西京居守，政以賄成，鄙哉，鄙哉，夫何足數！

translations.literal: Wensheng in relieving the siege of the eastern capital also exerted himself somewhat, but in holding the western capital his government was achieved through bribes—base, base! How can he be counted among the worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng did exert himself in lifting the siege of Luoyang, but his tenure at the western capital was built on bribery—contemptible, contemptible! He scarcely deserves mention!

sentences.zh: 劉權淮楚舊族，雄名早著，時逢擾攘，任等尉佗，遂能拒子邪言，足驗誠臣之節。

translations.literal: Liu Quan was of an old clan of the Huai and Chu region, his heroic name early renowned; when the age met turmoil his burden was like that of Wei Tuo, yet he could reject his son's wicked words—enough to prove a loyal minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan came from an old Huai-Chu family and was famed early; in troubled times his burden rivaled that of the Nanhai king Zhao Tuo, yet he refused his son's evil counsel—proof enough of a loyal minister's integrity.

sentences.zh: 李、薛並以驍武之用，當於有事之秋，致茲富貴，可謂自取。

translations.literal: Li and Xue both by use of fierce martial prowess, in an autumn when affairs were urgent, attained such wealth and honor—they may be said to have won it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue both owed their wealth and rank to martial prowess in a time of crisis—they largely earned what they got.

sentences.zh: 時迍遭躓，良有命乎！

translations.literal: That the times met obstruction and stumbling—was it truly fate!
translations.idiomatic: That they stumbled when the age turned against them—was it not fate after all!
